sentences.en: On the 27th of January 1848, Alexis de Tocqueville,
sentences.zh: 1848年1月27日，亚历克西·德·托克维尔，

sentences.en: French aristocrat and probably best known in the English-speaking world as the author of a groundbreaking study of democracy in America, addressed the Chamber of Deputies in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这位法国贵族，在英语世界中最广为人知的身份是那部开创性著作《论美国的民主》的作者，他在巴黎众议院发表了演讲。

sentences.en: And I will quote,
sentences.zh: 我来引用一下，

sentences.en: So, Dominic, momentous words, and as it turns out, prophetic, because that year of 1848 is commemorated as the year of revolutions.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这些话意义深远，事后证明更是具有预见性，因为1848年被后世铭记为革命之年。

sentences.en: The voice of prophecy, Tom, is often all the more resonant when it's read out in the voice of Chief Inspector Jacques Clouseau, as that was.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，预言的声音往往在用雅克·克鲁索探长的口吻读出来时，会显得格外响亮，就像刚才那样。

sentences.en: I thought you were going to say, in French, the language of diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你会说，是用外交语言——法语读出来的呢。

sentences.en: No, I wasn't going to say that.
sentences.zh: 不，我本来没打算那么说。

sentences.en: But yes, so we welcome Inspector Clouseau to the podcast for this episode about the 1848 revolutions.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以我们欢迎克卢索探长来到本期播客，一起聊聊1848年革命。

sentences.en: So, yeah, 1848 is remembered as the year of revolutions.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，1848年被铭记为革命之年。

sentences.en: And yet, of course, the question is, what was it all for and what did it achieve?
sentences.zh: 然而，问题当然在于，这一切究竟是为了什么？又取得了什么成果？

sentences.en: Because lots of people listening to this will have a sort of vague idea that 1848 is a bit like 1789 or 1968.
sentences.zh: 因为很多听众可能对1848年有一种模糊的印象，觉得它有点像1789年或1968年。

sentences.en: It's one of those dates that conjures up images of barricades and people on the streets.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让人联想到街垒和街头抗议人群的年份。

sentences.en: But it's more like 1968, though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但它其实更像1968年，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because actually the revolutions fizzle out and there's lots of kind of young people rushing around standing on barricades.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，这些革命最终都不了了之，尽管有很多年轻人四处奔走，站在街垒上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then lots of people shooting them.
sentences.zh: 然后就有很多人向他们开枪。

sentences.en: Yes, basically.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: And so the standard question about 1848 is why does it fail?
sentences.zh: 因此，关于1848年革命的一个标准问题是：它为什么会失败？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why do the revolutions fail?
sentences.zh: 为什么革命会失败？

sentences.en: However, in a groundbreaking study, Revolutionary Spring Fighting for a New World, 1848-1849, by the great Christopher Clarke, who is with us on the show.
sentences.zh: 然而，伟大的克里斯托弗·克拉克在开创性的著作《革命之春：为新世界而战，1848-1849》中对此进行了研究，他今天也来到了我们的节目现场。

sentences.en: The Regis Professor of History.
sentences.zh: 雷吉斯历史学教授。

sentences.en: Sir Christopher Clarke, Tom.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·克拉克爵士，汤姆。

sentences.en: We're very big on titles.
sentences.zh: 我们非常看重头衔。

sentences.en: Professor Sir Christopher Clarke.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·克拉克爵士教授。

sentences.en: And what's more, Tom, I know he's going to speak in a second, but just let me say we're particularly indebted to Chris for joining us because he's Australian.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，汤姆，我知道他马上就要发言了，但我只想说，我们特别感谢克里斯能加入我们，因为他是澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: And like a lot of people, he'll be in mourning because of the very recent passing of Dame Edna Everidge.
sentences.zh: 和许多人一样，他现在一定沉浸在悲痛之中，因为埃德娜·埃弗里奇女爵刚刚去世了。

sentences.en: Chris, was that a traumatic moment for you when you learned the news?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，得知这个消息时，你感到痛苦吗？

sentences.en: It was a sad moment, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，那是一个令人难过的时刻。

sentences.en: And I mean that, actually.
sentences.zh: 我是说真的。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I expect nothing less than the Regis Professor of History.
sentences.zh: 我对雷吉斯历史学教授的期待绝不仅限于此。

sentences.en: She was a very remarkable lady.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常了不起的女士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she spoke for us all.
sentences.zh: 她替我们所有人说出了心声。

sentences.en: I have to say, I didn't think that we'd be talking about Edna Everidge as our first topic.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，我没想到我们讨论的第一个话题竟然是埃德娜·埃弗里奇。

sentences.en: Dominic, can I go back to what I was going to say before you diverted us?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我能回到你打断我之前想说的话题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you're always welcome to do that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 当然，汤姆，随时欢迎。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the takeaway, I mean, there are lots of takeaways from this book, which is on an absolutely comprehensive scale.
sentences.zh: 所以重点是，我是说，这本书里有很多重点，它的涵盖范围绝对是非常全面的。

sentences.en: Because the takeaway that I found particularly intriguing is that you basically say that the whole question of did they succeed or fail is a nonsense question.
sentences.zh: 因为我发现一个特别有趣的结论是，你基本上认为“他们是成功了还是失败了”这个问题本身就是一个伪命题。

sentences.en: Towards the end of the book, you say, we don't say of an ocean storm, a solar flare or 16 days of heavy snowfall that they succeeded or fail.
sentences.zh: 在书的结尾处，你说，我们不会说一场海洋风暴、一次太阳耀斑或十六天的大雪是成功了还是失败了。

sentences.en: We simply measure their effects.
sentences.zh: 我们只是衡量它们的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that the problem with asking whether a revolution failed or succeeded is that, I mean, you might argue that, you know, look,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为询问一场革命是失败还是成功的问题在于，我的意思是，你可能会争辩说，你看，

sentences.en: we don't say that about a 16 days of heavy snowfall.
sentences.zh: 我们不会那样评价十六天的大雪。

sentences.en: But that's because snow is a natural phenomenon, whereas a revolution is a political phenomenon driven by a political intention.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为雪是一种自然现象，而革命是由政治意图驱动的政治现象。

sentences.en: And so we ought to be able to ask the question, was the intention fulfilled?
sentences.zh: 因此我们应该能够提出这个问题：意图实现了吗？

sentences.en: Is there a match between outcomes and intentions?
sentences.zh: 结果与意图之间是否匹配？

sentences.en: And if there is, we can say it was a success.
sentences.zh: 如果匹配，我们可以说它是成功的。

sentences.en: And if there isn't, we can say it was a failure.
sentences.zh: 如果不匹配，我们可以说它是失败的。

sentences.en: But the problem with that is that a revolution doesn't actually have an intention.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，革命实际上并没有一个统一的意图。

sentences.en: It has thousands of intentions.
sentences.zh: 它有成千上万种意图。

sentences.en: This revolution was not planned in advance.
sentences.zh: 这场革命并非事先策划好的。

sentences.en: It was very chaotic in the way it unfolded.
sentences.zh: 它的展开过程非常混乱。

sentences.en: A lot of entropy was built into the whole process.
sentences.zh: 整个过程中充满了大量的熵。

sentences.en: Groups and people kept seceding from the common enterprise.
sentences.zh: 团体和个人不断地从这项共同事业中脱离出来。

sentences.en: And so the question, what was the intention driving the revolution, has no answer.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于这场革命背后的意图是什么，这个问题并没有答案。

sentences.en: There were thousands of potentially conflicting intentions.
sentences.zh: 当时存在着成千上万种可能相互冲突的意图。

sentences.en: And so that makes the question, was it a success or not, a problematic question, because for some it was a huge success.
sentences.zh: 这使得“它是否成功”成了一个棘手的问题，因为对某些人来说，它取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: For others, it was a disastrous failure.
sentences.zh: 而对另一些人来说，这是一场灾难性的失败。

sentences.en: I mean, people died.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有人为此丧命。

sentences.en: They risked their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们冒着生命危险。

sentences.en: They risked everything for this revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们为这场革命赌上了一切。

sentences.en: So it makes more sense, it seems to me, to think of the revolution as a process.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，将革命视为一个过程会更有意义。

sentences.en: I mean, I like to think of it as a sort of as a collision chamber at the heart of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我喜欢把它想象成19世纪核心地带的一个碰撞室。

sentences.en: Everything fell into this chamber.
sentences.zh: 一切事物都落入了这间碰撞室。

sentences.en: It got crushed together with everything else under conditions of extreme density and pressure.
sentences.zh: 在极高的密度和压力下，它们与其他一切事物挤压在一起。

sentences.en: And then these entities showered out the other end of the process into the rest of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 随后，这些实体从过程的另一端喷涌而出，进入了19世纪的余下时光。

sentences.en: But everything was changed.
sentences.zh: 但一切都变了。

sentences.en: No one was the same shape.
sentences.zh: 没有人还是原来的样子。

sentences.en: No ideas were bent out of shape.
sentences.zh: 没有任何思想能保持原样。

sentences.en: Some things disappeared.
sentences.zh: 有些事物消失了。

sentences.en: Others appeared.
sentences.zh: 另一些事物出现了。

sentences.en: And so that's the way I like to think.
sentences.zh: 这就是我喜欢思考的方式。

sentences.en: I think we should be thinking about this revolution as a kind of engine of change at the heart of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该把这场革命看作是19世纪核心地带的一种变革引擎。

sentences.en: So if we go back to the very basics,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们回到最基础的层面来看，

sentences.en: your book starts with a couple of thematic chapters where you're talking about kind of poverty in Europe and the condition of people in the cities and people in the countryside and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你的书开头有几个主题章节，讨论了欧洲的贫困问题，以及城市和农村居民的生活状况等等。

sentences.en: But so Europe in the 1840s.
sentences.zh: 那么，19世纪40年代的欧洲是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: So this is the first decade of the life of Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 那是维多利亚女王统治的第一个十年。

sentences.en: Railways are beginning to come in.
sentences.zh: 铁路开始兴起。

sentences.en: It's not yet a landscape completely transformed by the telegraph, let's say.
sentences.zh: 可以说，当时的景观还没有被电报完全改变。

sentences.en: So in some ways it feels, if you're living in a little village somewhere in the middle of Poland, well, what's now Poland or France or something,
sentences.zh: 所以从某些方面来看，如果你住在波兰、法国或其他地方的某个小村庄里，

sentences.en: it probably feels like a very sleepy world.
sentences.zh: 那里的生活感觉可能非常宁静。

sentences.en: But in the cities, there's a tremendous sense of velocity, exchange of ideas, new technology.
sentences.zh: 但在城市里，却有着一种巨大的速度感、思想交流和新技术带来的冲击。

sentences.en: But Europe in the 1840s, what is it about Europe in the 1840s that makes it?
sentences.zh: 但19世纪40年代的欧洲，究竟是什么让它变得如此特别？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not an ancien regime.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它已经不再是旧制度时期了。

sentences.en: So what is it that explains the sort of, why is it a revolutionary tinderbox, as it were?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是什么解释了它为何会成为所谓的“革命火药桶”呢？

sentences.en: I mean, that's a terrible cliche, but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来是个陈词滥调，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: Well, it's a revolutionary tinderbox for lots of different reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它之所以成为革命火药桶，原因有很多。

sentences.en: I mean, one is the point you've already mentioned that, you know, a lot of people are under very high levels of social and economic stress.
sentences.zh: 首先就是你刚才提到的，很多人承受着极高的社会和经济压力。

sentences.en: And this stress isn't a constant.
sentences.zh: 而且这种压力并非一成不变。

sentences.en: It sort of pulses.
sentences.zh: 它是有波动的。

sentences.en: It comes at some moments and then recedes.
sentences.zh: 有时出现，有时又会消退。

sentences.en: Because this is a system, it's not that everybody's, that there's a generalized shortage of food.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个系统，并不是说每个人都面临普遍的粮食短缺。

sentences.en: There's plenty of food to go around.
sentences.zh: 实际上粮食供应充足。

sentences.en: But every so often, there are disruptions to the food supply, as indeed we're experiencing again today.
sentences.zh: 但每隔一段时间，粮食供应就会出现中断，正如我们今天所经历的那样。

sentences.en: That's one of the parallels between then and now.
sentences.zh: 这也是当时与现在相似的地方之一。

sentences.en: And these short-term disruptions to the food supply can push people in huge numbers over the edge, over the brink of subsistence into real crisis.
sentences.zh: 而这些短期的粮食供应中断，可以将大量人口推向绝境，从勉强糊口跌入真正的危机。

sentences.en: And this, one of the moments at which this happens is 1846-47.
sentences.zh: 而1846到1847年就是发生这种情况的时刻之一。

sentences.en: There's a very bad, very cold harveSt.
sentences.zh: 那一年收成极差，天气非常寒冷。

sentences.en: The price of grains shoots up.
sentences.zh: 粮价飙升。

sentences.en: And because most of what most poorer people eat is bread or grain-based food of one kind or another, they can't substitute for it with other foods.
sentences.zh: 由于贫困人口的主要食物是面包或谷物制品，他们无法用其他食物来替代。

sentences.en: They can't just eat chicken instead or cake, as famously Marie Antoinette had once suggested they should do in the context of an earlier revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们不能像玛丽·安托瓦内特在早期革命背景下那句名言所建议的那样，去吃鸡肉或蛋糕。

sentences.en: So, they're pushed into a genuine state of emergency.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们被推入了真正的紧急状态。

sentences.en: And that has the effect of bringing people onto the streets.
sentences.zh: 这导致人们纷纷走上街头。

sentences.en: It means there are a lot of, you know, discontented, angry, resentful apprentices, artisans, and so on, available in the big cities for a tumult, if a tumult should arise.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在大城市里，有许多不满、愤怒和怨恨的学徒、工匠等，一旦骚乱爆发，他们随时可能参与其中。

sentences.en: So, that's part of the background.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是背景的一部分。

sentences.en: But there's also the fact that this is a continent which is incubating lots of different political movements.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个事实是，这片大陆正在孕育着许多不同的政治运动。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the fascinating things about the 1830s and 40s in Europe is the extraordinary political biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 19世纪30和40年代的欧洲，最迷人的地方之一就是其非凡的政治生物多样性。

sentences.en: There are several hundred different kinds of socialism.
sentences.zh: 当时有几百种不同形式的社会主义。

sentences.en: I mean, people talk about socialism, but the term has no fixed meaning.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论社会主义，但这个词并没有固定的含义。

sentences.en: And Marx is around and he's commenting on things in a sort of very brilliant and mordant and polemical and rather one-sided way.
sentences.zh: 马克思当时也在活跃，他以一种非常犀利、尖刻、好辩且略显片面的方式评论着时事。

sentences.en: But Marxism has not yet dominated this spectrum of socialism.
sentences.zh: 但马克思主义当时尚未主导整个社会主义光谱。

sentences.en: So, an immense diversity of left-wing thinking about, you know, how to live a better life,
sentences.zh: 因此，左翼思想呈现出巨大的多样性，探讨着如何过上更好的生活，

sentences.en: how to create a form of state order which allows humans to flourish and so on and so forth in the broadest possible sense.
sentences.zh: 如何创造一种能让人类蓬勃发展的国家秩序，等等，从最广泛的意义上来说。

sentences.en: And then there are many liberalisMs.
sentences.zh: 此外还有许多自由主义。

sentences.en: The liberals are the people who want to somehow balance, you know, authoritarian structures like absolute monarchy, of which there are plenty in Europe in the 1830s and 40s,
sentences.zh: 自由主义者试图在专制结构（如19世纪30和40年代欧洲随处可见的绝对君主制）与议会权力之间寻找平衡。

sentences.en: with the power of parliaments.
sentences.zh: 而保守派则开始思考，在每个人都能感受到的变革浪潮面前，如何保留旧制度中那些有价值的东西。

sentences.en: And then there are conservatives who are starting to think about how you preserve what is valuable about the Ancien Régime in the face of this tide of change that everyone recognizes is there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，连梅特涅都说，我们必须筑起一道大坝来遏制洪水。

sentences.en: I mean, even Metternich speaks of, he says, we must build a dam to contain the flood.
sentences.zh: 在这一表述中，我们已经看到，这位作为大陆元老的政治家，

sentences.en: And already in that formulation, we see that, you know, this man who's the kind of elder statesman of the continent,
sentences.zh: 这位在其职业生涯中曾担任奥地利帝国总理或外交大臣的人，即使是他也意识到，存在着这种如河流般的变革趋势，

sentences.en: the chancellor or the foreign minister at various points in his career of the Austrian Empire, even he recognizes that there's this river-like flow of change,
sentences.zh: 你要么顺流而下，要么试图筑坝阻挡。

sentences.en: which you're either going to swim with or try and dam in and stop.
sentences.zh: 每个人都承认这种趋势的存在。

sentences.en: And everybody acknowledges that it's there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个大家都意识到冲突与变革潜力的时代，但人们并不确定该如何实现。

sentences.en: So, it's a time when everybody recognizes the potential for conflict and change, but people aren't sure about how this can be achieved.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那些身居高位的人，看起来并不特别压迫，也不怎么专制。

sentences.en: And the people who are at the top, to my way of thinking, they don't look peculiarly repressive or indeed authoritarian.
sentences.zh: 比如法国的路易-菲利普国王，他被誉为“资产阶级国王”。

sentences.en: So, if you take France, for example, King Louis-Philippe, he is famously the kind of bourgeois king.
sentences.zh: 每个人都嘲笑他。

sentences.en: Everybody makes fun of him.
sentences.zh: 他们说他长得像个梨。

sentences.en: They say he looks like a pear.
sentences.zh: 他看起来是个好人。

sentences.en: He seems like a nice guy.
sentences.zh: 就像个中产阶级的英国人。

sentences.en: He's like a sort of middle-class Englishman.
sentences.zh: 他有基佐，我想那是他的首相吧，非常文明、理智，某种程度上是这样。

sentences.en: He's got Guizzo, who I think is his prime minister, isn't he, who's very civilized, cerebral, kind of.
sentences.zh: 是的，他写了70多本书。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wrote over 70 books.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在选角拍电影，这些人并不是那种令人满意的、压迫性的反派，不是那种戴着高帽的坏蛋。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, you know, if you're casting a film, these are not people who make satisfying, repressive villains, top-hatted villains or something.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得你可能会选汤姆·汉克斯来演路易-菲利普，而不是选个坏蛋。

sentences.en: No, you'd probably choose Tom Hanks to play Louis-Philippe, I think, rather than some bad guy.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 那么，他们究竟做错了什么呢？

sentences.en: So, what is it they are doing wrong, as it were?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Well, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 事实上，基佐并没有做错太多事。

sentences.en: Actually, Guizzo was not doing a huge amount wrong.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，在很多方面，这其实是一个相当成功的政府。

sentences.en: It was actually, in many ways, quite a successful government, as you say it.
sentences.zh: 但这个政府最终陷入了与媒体的战争之中。

sentences.en: But it was a government that had managed to wind up in a kind of war with the media.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在，当时有一股针对君主制的猛烈抨击浪潮，指责国王腐败、令人作呕，

sentences.en: That's one of the problems, that there was this shower, a kind of flood of invective against the monarchy, which denounced the king as corrupt, as disgusting,
sentences.zh: 把他的脸画成梨的形象，等等。

sentences.en: the image of his face as a pear, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这听起来并不算什么。

sentences.en: It wasn't – it sounds rather initiative.
sentences.zh: 那只是一种可爱的水果，但实际上，我想到了一幅特定的漫画，

sentences.en: It's just, you know, that rather likable fruit, but in fact, you know, there were – I'm thinking now of a particular cartoon,
sentences.zh: 那幅漫画在19世纪40年代初出现时被广泛转载，画中一个梨状物体坐在一个叫“糖蜜桶”的东西上，

sentences.en: which is widely reprinted when it appeared in the early 1840s, a cartoon which shows a pear-like object seated on top of a thing called a coque du melasse,
sentences.zh: 那是一种装糖蜜的桶。

sentences.en: a sort of barrel for the molasses.
sentences.zh: 那是一种装糖蜜的桶。

sentences.en: But you have to remember that molasses was the sort of slang word for excrement in French.
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，在法语中，“糖蜜”曾是排泄物的俚语。

sentences.en: And underneath it is a royal-looking chair.
sentences.zh: 而在它下面是一把看起来很皇家的椅子。

sentences.en: And this horrible contraption is supposed to be the king, you know, a pear-shaped head and a barrel full of excrement and a nice sort of antique chair.
sentences.zh: 这个可怕的装置被认为是国王，你知道的，梨形的脑袋，装满排泄物的桶，还有一把不错的古董椅。

sentences.en: And it's being gawked at by a group of French people who are standing around it, looking at it disgustedly.
sentences.zh: 一群法国人围在它周围，厌恶地盯着它看。

sentences.en: That's the sort of image of the regime.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个政权的形象。

sentences.en: And at the same time, there's the problem of who is represented in the representative politics of this monarchy.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，还存在一个问题，即谁在这个君主制的代议制政治中得到了代表。

sentences.en: It is a constitutional monarchy, and that's one of the weird things.
sentences.zh: 这是一个君主立宪制国家，这是最奇怪的事情之一。

sentences.en: You know, they've had a revolution in 1830.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在1830年经历了一场革命。

sentences.en: They've revised the constitution that they got in 1814.
sentences.zh: 他们修订了1814年获得的宪法。

sentences.en: So it is a constitutional, in that sense, a liberal order.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，它是一个宪政的、自由的秩序。

sentences.en: But the constitution enfranchises fewer than 2% of the population.
sentences.zh: 但宪法赋予的选举权不到人口的2%。

sentences.en: And this is a male franchise only, but it's a tiny, tiny fragment of the wealthieSt.
sentences.zh: 而且这仅限于男性选举权，但这只是最富有阶层中极小、极小的一部分。

sentences.en: And obviously, in France, there is the memory of the primal revolution.
sentences.zh: 显然，在法国，人们对原始革命记忆犹新。

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The 1789 revolution, the memory of the terror, the memory of the Napoleonic regime.
sentences.zh: 1789年的革命，对恐怖时期的记忆，对拿破仑政权的记忆。

sentences.en: So France is peculiarly associated with revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以法国与革命有着特殊的联系。

sentences.en: But the thing about 1848 is that it's not confined to France and that it spreads across.
sentences.zh: 但1848年的特别之处在于，它不仅局限于法国，而且蔓延开来。

sentences.en: In fact, I mean, in 1848, it's not initially France where a revolution breaks out, is it?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的意思是，在1848年，革命最初并不是在法国爆发的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 是在西西里。

sentences.en: It is in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 确实是在西西里。

sentences.en: In fact, I mean, you say the French have this revolution in their minds.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的意思是，你说法国人脑子里有这场革命。

sentences.en: Of course they do.
sentences.zh: 他们当然有。

sentences.en: It's playing like an old film at the backs of their heads.
sentences.zh: 它就像一部老电影在他们的脑海中不断回放。

sentences.en: But it's doing that right across Europe.
sentences.zh: 但这在整个欧洲都在发生。

sentences.en: I mean, Europeans in general, this is something they have in common.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，欧洲人普遍都有这种共同点。

sentences.en: They have a lot in common in this era, perhaps more even than they do today.
sentences.zh: 在这个时代，他们有很多共同点，甚至可能比今天还要多。

sentences.en: They have common stories and narratives.
sentences.zh: 他们有共同的故事和叙事。

sentences.en: And one of these narratives is the narrative of this revolution in France, of its sequence of phases.
sentences.zh: 其中一个叙事就是法国这场革命的叙事，以及它各个阶段的演变。

sentences.en: You know, the liberal revolution followed by the Jacobin terrorist experiment, followed by the directory, followed by Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自由主义革命之后是雅各宾派的恐怖实验，接着是督政府，然后是拿破仑。

sentences.en: They all have that story in their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们脑子里都有那个故事。

sentences.en: So they all have that script available.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都有那个现成的剧本。

sentences.en: But that script isn't necessarily a sort of recipe for revolution, because the memory of revolution is also an argument against revolution.
sentences.zh: 但那个剧本并不一定就是革命的处方，因为对革命的记忆也是反对革命的论据。

sentences.en: Those who remember the Jacobin terror, for example, say, let's not take any risks.
sentences.zh: 例如，那些记得雅各宾恐怖统治的人会说，我们不要冒任何风险。

sentences.en: I mean, Guizot's father was executed when he was five years old.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基佐的父亲在他五岁时就被处决了。

sentences.en: His father was executed by the guillotine in Nîmes.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲在尼姆被断头台处决。

sentences.en: And he remembered that, of course, it was a traumatic memory,
sentences.zh: 他当然记得那件事，那是一段创伤性的记忆，

sentences.en: and he remained deeply opposed to the death penalty and opposed to violent or extremist political experiments of any kind.
sentences.zh: 他始终坚决反对死刑，反对任何形式的暴力或极端政治实验。

sentences.en: So he was a conservative in one way and would fall when the 1848 revolution broke out.
sentences.zh: 所以他在某种程度上是一个保守派，在1848年革命爆发时他倒台了。

sentences.en: But he was also someone who remembered very vividly the French revolution.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一个对法国大革命记忆犹新的人。

sentences.en: But he remembered it as a lesson against risking experiments.
sentences.zh: 但他将其视为反对冒险实验的教训。

sentences.en: So when we get to, let's say, the end of 1847, there's been bad harvests, there's been food shortages.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们来到1847年底时，发生了歉收，出现了粮食短缺。

sentences.en: So to give us, I mean, just to remind people about the map of Europe, you have France.
sentences.zh: 为了让我们，我的意思是，只是为了提醒人们欧洲的地图，你有法国。

sentences.en: There is no Germany.
sentences.zh: 没有德国。

sentences.en: Germany is fragmented.
sentences.zh: 德国是四分五裂的。

sentences.en: There's a kind of German confederation, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 有一种德意志邦联，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there's a loose confederation of German states called the Deutsche Bund, which consists of 39 sovereign states.
sentences.zh: 是的，有一个由39个主权国家组成的松散的德意志邦联，称为德意志邦联。

sentences.en: Switzerland is still a very loosely confederated state.
sentences.zh: 瑞士仍然是一个非常松散的邦联国家。

sentences.en: It's not really a state at all.
sentences.zh: 它根本算不上一个国家。

sentences.en: In fact, the cantons are virtually independent with a very weak government, which moves from one place to another.
sentences.zh: 事实上，各州几乎是独立的，政府非常软弱，而且经常搬迁。

sentences.en: There is no Italy.
sentences.zh: 没有意大利。

sentences.en: And North Italy is ruled by Austria.
sentences.zh: 北意大利由奥地利统治。

sentences.en: Northeastern Italy is ruled by Austria.
sentences.zh: 意大利东北部由奥地利统治。

sentences.en: Lombardy and Venetia are both under Austrian control.
sentences.zh: 伦巴第和威尼托都在奥地利的控制之下。

sentences.en: Piedmont is independent.
sentences.zh: 皮埃蒙特是独立的。

sentences.en: And then you have the papal states and the kingdom of the two Sicilies.
sentences.zh: 然后是教皇国和两西西里王国。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's a crucial thing as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这也是关键的一点，不是吗？

sentences.en: That the pope is a temporal ruler as well as a spiritual ruler.
sentences.zh: 教皇既是世俗统治者，也是精神统治者。

sentences.en: The pope has his own state.
sentences.zh: 教皇有他自己的国家。

sentences.en: That's another exotic feature of the European map at this time.
sentences.zh: 这是当时欧洲地图上另一个异国情调的特征。

sentences.en: And another exotic sort of piece of local color is the kingdom of the two Sicilies in the south, which is the bizarrely named amalgam of Sicily, the island,
sentences.zh: 另一个充满异国情调的地方色彩是南部的两西西里王国，这是一个名字古怪的混合体，由西西里岛，

sentences.en: and of the Neapolitan mainland of the south of Italy, south of the papal states.
sentences.zh: 以及教皇国以南的意大利南部那不勒斯大陆组成。

sentences.en: So there are lots of states that don't exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多国家已经不存在了。

sentences.en: On the other hand, there is a state that didn't exist and does now, and that's Poland.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，有一个曾经不存在但现在存在的国家，那就是波兰。

sentences.en: Poland is nowhere on the map because in the 18th century it had been partitioned by its three neighboring states, the Prussians, the Austrians and the Russians.
sentences.zh: 地图上找不到波兰，因为在18世纪，它被其三个邻国——普鲁士、奥地利和俄罗斯瓜分了。

sentences.en: So there's no Polish state, but there is very much a Polish nation with a memory of what it was like to inhabit the great Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 所以没有波兰国家，但确实存在一个波兰民族，他们记得居住在伟大的波兰-立陶宛联邦是什么样子。

sentences.en: And that, again, is a factor in the revolution because these unhappy poles are going to play a very important role in carrying the agenda of revolution from one place to another.
sentences.zh: 这再次成为革命的一个因素，因为这些不满的波兰人将在把革命议程从一个地方带到另一个地方的过程中发挥非常重要的作用。

sentences.en: And so, Chris, that is one further element.
sentences.zh: 所以，克里斯，这是又一个因素。

sentences.en: So you've talked about the legacy of the French Revolution and the social pressures, but this is also an age of nationalism.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了法国大革命的遗产和社会压力，但这也是一个民族主义的时代。

sentences.en: And you have a brilliant description that its effect on the revolutions of 1880 as a whole was like that of heroin on the body and mind of an addict.
sentences.zh: 你有一个精彩的描述，说它对1848年整体革命的影响，就像海洛因对瘾君子身心的影响一样。

sentences.en: So that is something that is enhancing the revolutionary spirit, but also turning it into courses that the powers that be don't recognize.
sentences.zh: 所以这既增强了革命精神，也使其转向了当权者无法识别的轨道。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Nationalism is the most difficult theme for 1848 because after 1848 happened, the memory of 1848 was processed by the national movements of Italy, Germany, France,
sentences.zh: 民族主义是1848年最困难的主题，因为在1848年事件发生后，1848年的记忆被意大利、德国、法国的民族运动所加工，

sentences.en: later of Hungary and so on.
sentences.zh: 后来是匈牙利等等。

sentences.en: And it's still part of the national memory of Hungary where Viktor Orban never fails to mention the struggles for Hungarian freedom in 1848,
sentences.zh: 它仍然是匈牙利民族记忆的一部分，维克多·欧尔班从不放过提及1848年匈牙利争取自由的斗争的机会，

sentences.en: always distorting them and turning them, obviously, to contemporary objectives.
sentences.zh: 显然总是歪曲它们，并将它们转向当代的政治目标。

sentences.en: So nationalism is part of what shapes what we remember about 1848.
sentences.zh: 所以民族主义是我们对1848年记忆的一部分。

sentences.en: And so we have to think our way past that lens, lensing effect, if you like, and put ourselves in a world where nationalism is present and has a drug-like effect on people,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们必须跳出那种透镜效应，如果你愿意的话，把自己置身于一个民族主义存在并对人们产生类似毒品影响的世界中，

sentences.en: but it's a periodic effect.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种周期性的影响。

sentences.en: People can become extremely excited.
sentences.zh: 人们会变得极其兴奋。

sentences.en: They wear national clothing when they come together and they see everybody else wearing their red caps or their blue cinched jackets or whatever it is,
sentences.zh: 当他们聚在一起时，他们会穿上民族服装，看到其他人戴着红帽子或穿着蓝色束腰夹克，或者其他什么东西，

sentences.en: whether they're Croats or Hungarians or Germans wearing national costume.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是克罗地亚人、匈牙利人还是穿着民族服装的德国人。

sentences.en: The effect on people is absolutely overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 这对人们的影响是绝对压倒性的。

sentences.en: The emotional power of these moments of patriotic feeling is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这些爱国情感时刻的情感力量是非凡的。

sentences.en: So in one way, it brings people together and it submerges them in a larger collective self.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，它把人们聚集在一起，并将他们淹没在一个更大的集体自我中。

sentences.en: On the other hand, it also divides them because, you know, the Hungarians, when they rise up against the Austrians,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，它也分裂了他们，因为你知道，当匈牙利人反抗奥地利人时，

sentences.en: they find themselves dealing with national movements of the Slovaks, the Croats and the Romanians, people who are minorities within the Kingdom of Hungary,
sentences.zh: 他们发现自己要应对斯洛伐克人、克罗地亚人和罗马尼亚人的民族运动，这些人是匈牙利王国境内的少数民族，

sentences.en: who don't wish to be ruled by an independent Hungary, but would rather be ruled from more distant, more impartial Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望被独立的匈牙利统治，而宁愿被更遥远、更公正的维也纳统治。

sentences.en: So it's a very complex presence.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常复杂的现象。

sentences.en: And the other interesting thing about nationalism, and nationalism has this peculiar, almost magical effect, that it comes with the illusion that it is old.
sentences.zh: 关于民族主义的另一个有趣之处在于，民族主义有一种奇特的、几乎是神奇的效果，它带有一种它是古老的错觉。

sentences.en: So when people experience national feeling, they feel they're inheriting something from the Middle Ages or even before that, something very, very ancient.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们体验到民族情感时，他们觉得他们继承了中世纪甚至更早之前的东西，一些非常、非常古老的东西。

sentences.en: Ancient Magyars or whoever it might be.
sentences.zh: 古老的马扎尔人或其他什么人。

sentences.en: Ancient Magyars, exactly.
sentences.zh: 古老的马扎尔人，没错。

sentences.en: Magyars spreading out in the 11th century across the Danubian plain and so on.
sentences.zh: 11世纪散布在多瑙河平原上的马扎尔人等等。

sentences.en: Whereas, in fact, these nationalist experiences are very new.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实上，这些民族主义体验是非常新的。

sentences.en: They're created by newspapers and communication networks, and the national clothing people wear is mostly an invented retro style that people have come up with in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 它们是由报纸和通信网络创造的，人们穿的民族服装大多是人们在19世纪想出来的发明出来的复古风格。

sentences.en: Like the kilts, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像苏格兰短裙一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Like the kilts.
sentences.zh: 就像苏格兰短裙一样。

sentences.en: Invented traditions, exactly.
sentences.zh: 发明出来的传统，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, on that topic, you have a wonderful quote by Metternich, the kind of the conservatives, conservative, the Austrian foreign minister,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于这个话题，你引用了梅特涅的一句精彩的话，他是保守派中的保守派，奥地利外交大臣，

sentences.en: Tukant Rosetsky, who's basically the military commander with responsibility for Austrian possessions in North Italy.
sentences.zh: 图坎特·罗塞茨基，他基本上是负责奥地利在北意大利领地的军事指挥官。

sentences.en: And he's writing in August 1847, so just before the explosion, that if the past imposed great efforts on us, it was at least better than the present.
sentences.zh: 他在1847年8月，也就是爆炸前夕写道，如果过去强加给我们巨大的努力，至少比现在要好。

sentences.en: You and I know how to fight against bodies, but against phantoms, material force can achieve nothing.
sentences.zh: 你和我知道如何与肉体战斗，但面对幻影，物质力量一无所获。

sentences.en: And today we are fighting phantoms everywhere.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们到处都在与幻影战斗。

sentences.en: Is he expressing something that is commonly felt by the elites in this period?
sentences.zh: 他是否表达了这一时期精英阶层普遍感受到的东西？

sentences.en: That they're aware, of course, of the revolutionary potential because they have the history of the French Revolution,
sentences.zh: 他们当然意识到革命的潜力，因为他们有法国大革命的历史，

sentences.en: but that the manifestation of it is something strange, new that they don't know how to fight, they don't know how to cope with.
sentences.zh: 但其表现形式是一种奇怪的、新的东西，他们不知道如何战斗，不知道如何应对。

sentences.en: Yes, and nationalism is a phantom and a terrifying phantom for Metternich because he's a senior politician in a multinational empire.
sentences.zh: 是的，民族主义对梅特涅来说是一个幻影，一个可怕的幻影，因为他是一个多民族帝国的高级政治家。

sentences.en: I mean, we would call it multinational now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在会称它为多民族帝国。

sentences.en: Nobody would have used that word then, but it's a commonwealth of ethnicities with, you know, 11 or 12 different major languages and many other dialects beside.
sentences.zh: 当时没人会用那个词，但它是一个民族共同体，你知道，有11或12种不同的主要语言，还有许多其他方言。

sentences.en: So, for an empire like that, nationalism is a dissolving poison.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于这样一个帝国来说，民族主义是一种溶解的毒药。

sentences.en: It will simply tear the thing apart.
sentences.zh: 它会直接把这个东西撕碎。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he's right to see nationalism as a threat.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他把民族主义视为威胁是正确的。

sentences.en: It's also a threat in another way, and that is that although it may not voice a principled objection to monarchy, nationalists can also be monarchists.
sentences.zh: 它在另一方面也是一种威胁，那就是虽然它可能不会对君主制提出原则性的反对，但民族主义者也可能是保皇党。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, nationalism proposes implicitly, at least, that the center of authority, the kind of center of gravity of a population is not its dynasty, but its ethnic substance.
sentences.zh: 然而，民族主义至少隐含地提出，权威的中心，即人口的重心，不是其王朝，而是其民族实体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that means the people.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人民。

sentences.en: So, it's a way of taking power from the crown and placing it in the heart of an ethnic group, which is, of course, disturbing to the holders of traditional power in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种从王室手中夺取权力并将其置于民族群体核心的方式，这当然让欧洲传统权力的持有者感到不安。

sentences.en: So, to sort of turn to the narrative, I mean, Tom mentioned that the first sort of flashpoint is actually not in France, but in Sicily, in Palermo.
sentences.zh: 所以，转到叙事上来，我的意思是，汤姆提到第一个爆发点实际上不在法国，而是在西西里，在巴勒莫。

sentences.en: I think one of the things that your account of it does quite brilliantly is to show all the contingencies and all the twists and turns.
sentences.zh: 我认为你对它的描述非常出色的一点是，展示了所有的偶然性和所有的曲折。

sentences.en: And France is the big, I mean, France is the big one, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而法国是最大的，我的意思是，法国是最大的一个，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, that starts in the first weeks of 1848, and it's all to do with banquets, the cancellation of political banquets,
sentences.zh: 所以，那始于1848年的最初几周，一切都与宴会有关，政治宴会的取消，

sentences.en: a very sort of banal trigger, you one would think, for a continental-wide upsurge of popular enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 一个非常平庸的导火索，你会认为，对于一场全大陆范围的民众热情高涨来说。

sentences.en: One could sort of quip and say, you know, only France would rise up in revolution because of a cancelled banquet.
sentences.zh: 人们可以打趣说，你知道，只有法国才会因为取消宴会而爆发革命。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's true, the Parisian revolution is important.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这是真的，巴黎革命很重要。

sentences.en: But, you know, think about that speech by Tocqueville, which Tom cited at the beginning, or Inspector Clouseau cited,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，想想托克维尔在开头引用的那段演讲，或者克鲁索探长引用的那段，

sentences.en: that, you know, Tocqueville can make this prophecy because he's been reading the papers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，托克维尔能做出这个预言是因为他一直在看报纸。

sentences.en: And the papers are full of tumults from all over Europe by the end of January, which is when he speaks, the 27th of January.
sentences.zh: 到一月底，也就是他发言的时候，1月27日，报纸上到处都是来自欧洲各地的骚乱消息。

sentences.en: By the end of January, there's news coming up from the south of Italy, from Palermo and from Naples, but also from Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 到一月底，有来自意大利南部、巴勒莫和那不勒斯的消息，也有来自瑞士的消息。

sentences.en: I mean, Switzerland had already had a civil war in the previous year, the Sonderbundkrieg, as it's called in Switzerland, which creates, you know, a modern constitutional state.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，瑞士在前一年已经发生了一场内战，即瑞士所谓的“独立同盟战争”，这创造了一个现代宪政国家。

sentences.en: In fact, it creates the Switzerland we have today.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它创造了我们今天拥有的瑞士。

sentences.en: The modern Switzerland today is born in 1848.
sentences.zh: 今天的现代瑞士诞生于1848年。

sentences.en: So that's already been happening, and it's widely reported in the press.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经发生了，并且在媒体上被广泛报道。

sentences.en: The horizons of press reportage are very much European.
sentences.zh: 新闻报道的视野非常欧洲化。

sentences.en: They're not, you know, siloed in national or regional or territorial silos.
sentences.zh: 它们不是，你知道，被隔离在国家、地区或领土的筒仓里。

sentences.en: They're very much looking to the extent of the continent.
sentences.zh: 它们非常关注整个大陆的范围。

sentences.en: And, you know, Tocqueville is drawing on that when he says, you know, this storm that you see now on the horizon is coming for us.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，托克维尔在说“你现在在地平线上看到的这场风暴正向我们袭来”时，正是借鉴了这一点。

sentences.en: So the contagiousness of these tumults is already recognizable by the time the revolution happens in Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以，当巴黎发生革命时，这些骚乱的传染性已经是显而易见的了。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about this year, Dominic mentioned the contingent sort of happenstance quality of this.
sentences.zh: 关于这一年有趣的事情是，多米尼克提到了这种偶然的、碰巧的性质。

sentences.en: It is odd how virtually every one of these uprisings begins almost kind of by accident.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，几乎每一场起义几乎都是偶然开始的。

sentences.en: So the one in Palermo starts when a poster appears, which simply says, you know, a few days there's going to be a revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以巴勒莫的那场起义始于一张海报的出现，上面简单地写着，你知道，几天后就会有一场革命。

sentences.en: Get prepared.
sentences.zh: 准备好。

sentences.en: Sicilians, rise up.
sentences.zh: 西西里人，起来吧。

sentences.en: Your moment of freedom has arrived.
sentences.zh: 你们自由的时刻已经到来。

sentences.en: Signed, Comitato Revoluzionario, the Revolutionary Committee.
sentences.zh: 签名：革命委员会。

sentences.en: Now, there was no Revolutionary Committee.
sentences.zh: 现在，根本没有所谓的革命委员会。

sentences.en: This whole thing was a prank put up by a guy called Baniasco who just thought, I think maybe people will rise up if I put a, you know, a sheet on a wall.
sentences.zh: 整件事是一个叫巴尼亚斯科的人搞的恶作剧，他只是想，我想如果我在墙上贴一张纸，也许人们会起来反抗。

sentences.en: So he did that.
sentences.zh: 所以他那样做了。

sentences.en: And sure enough, on the day that the revolution had been announced for, everybody did turn up to see what was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 果然，在宣布革命的那一天，每个人都出现了，想看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: And nothing happened because nothing had been planned, except that the troops had been doubled and tripled throughout Palermo.
sentences.zh: 结果什么也没发生，因为什么都没计划好，只是整个巴勒莫的军队被增加了一倍和三倍。

sentences.en: So there are many more troops than usual.
sentences.zh: 所以军队比平时多了很多。

sentences.en: And inevitably, you know, a clash broke out between the people and the troops.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，你知道，民众和军队之间爆发了冲突。

sentences.en: And that was the beginning of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 那就是革命的开端。

sentences.en: And something very similar happened in Paris.
sentences.zh: 巴黎也发生了非常相似的事情。

sentences.en: You know, shots fired by accident and so on led to a massive upheaval.
sentences.zh: 你知道，意外走火等等引发了大规模的动荡。

sentences.en: Lamartine, a French sort of, you know, liberal slash radical politician, very much involved in the February Revolution,
sentences.zh: 拉马丁，一位法国的，你知道，自由派兼激进派政治家，深度参与了二月革命，

sentences.en: and said it was almost as if the revolution was engendered by the curiosity of the crowds that had gathered to see if a revolution would happen.
sentences.zh: 他说，这几乎就像是革命是由那些聚集在一起想看看会不会发生革命的人群的好奇心所引发的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But also, it's a fair to say in the case of Paris, you were talking about the silent film playing in people's heads, that Louis Philippe doesn't want to be Louis XVI.
sentences.zh: 但也可以说，就巴黎的情况而言，你刚才提到的那种人们脑海中播放的默片，路易·菲利普不想成为路易十六。

sentences.en: As soon as the revolution breaks out, it's precisely because he has the memory of 1789 and what happened afterwards.
sentences.zh: 革命一爆发，正是因为他有1789年及其后发生之事的记忆。

sentences.en: So he's like, OK, I'm out of here.
sentences.zh: 所以他想，好吧，我得走了。

sentences.en: I'm gone.
sentences.zh: 我走了。

sentences.en: I'm abdicating.
sentences.zh: 我退位。

sentences.en: He's gone.
sentences.zh: 他走了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And he actually didn't need to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且他其实没必要这么做。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: He could have stuck it out, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想他本可以坚持下去的。

sentences.en: I mean, the main problem was that the French police in Paris, the municipal guards and the mobile guards and the national guard and the army, in fact,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，主要问题在于巴黎的法国警察、市政卫队、机动卫队、国民卫队以及军队，事实上，

sentences.en: had all been preparing for decades for a conspiratorial revolution organized by underground networks.
sentences.zh: 几十年来一直都在为地下网络组织的阴谋革命做准备。

sentences.en: And so they were going to concentrate on the areas of Paris where the trouble was starting and crush it there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们打算集中力量在巴黎骚乱开始的地区，并在那里镇压它。

sentences.en: And then, you know, the plan was all organized around the idea of a conspiratorially organized and planned revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，整个计划都是围绕着一场阴谋组织和策划的革命这一理念来制定的。

sentences.en: But what actually happened was more like a societal tsunami.
sentences.zh: 但实际发生的情况更像是一场社会海啸。

sentences.en: The society threw off the regime and decided it didn't fear the forces of order anymore and it didn't respect the government anymore.
sentences.zh: 社会抛弃了旧政权，决定不再畏惧秩序维护力量，也不再尊重政府。

sentences.en: And that's a really dangerous thing.
sentences.zh: 那真的是一件非常危险的事情。

sentences.en: And there was absolutely nothing that Louis Philippe, I mean, at one point, for example, it was impossible to deploy troops in Paris because the crowds were simply too large.
sentences.zh: 路易·菲利普对此完全无能为力，我的意思是，比如在某个时刻，由于人群实在太大，根本无法在巴黎部署军队。

sentences.en: The troops couldn't move through them.
sentences.zh: 军队无法穿过人群。

sentences.en: So they simply faced a situation that they were not prepared to handle and were incapable of handling.
sentences.zh: 所以他们面对的是一种他们未曾准备好也无法处理的局面。

sentences.en: And quite wisely, Louis Philippe decided, well, really, my time's up and skedaddled.
sentences.zh: 路易·菲利普很明智地决定，好吧，我的时间到了，然后溜之大吉。

sentences.en: So France is obviously, as Dominic said, the big one.
sentences.zh: 所以正如多米尼克所说，法国显然是重头戏。

sentences.en: It's the great monarchy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的君主国。

sentences.en: It's got the history of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 它拥有法国大革命的历史。

sentences.en: Narratives of revolution in France are something that people can comprehend and understand.
sentences.zh: 法国的革命叙事是人们能够理解和领会的。

sentences.en: But what then happens is that revolution starts to spread in a cascade effect across Europe.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生的是，革命开始在欧洲产生连锁反应。

sentences.en: And I don't want to frighten people because we're going to have a break in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我不想吓唬大家，因为我们马上就要休息一下了。

sentences.en: But this is what you say about this process.
sentences.zh: 但这就是你所说的这个过程。

sentences.en: From the beginning of March 1848, it becomes impossible to trace the revolutions as a linear sequence from one theatre of turbulence to the next.
sentences.zh: 从1848年3月初开始，就不可能再把这些革命视为从一个动荡剧场到下一个剧场的线性序列了。

sentences.en: We enter the fission phase in which almost simultaneous detonations create complex feedback loops.
sentences.zh: 我们进入了裂变阶段，几乎同时发生的引爆创造了复杂的反馈回路。

sentences.en: The narrative bursts its banks.
sentences.zh: 叙事冲破了堤岸。

sentences.en: The historian bespares.
sentences.zh: 历史学家绝望了。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: So I think we should take a break at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们现在应该休息一下。

sentences.en: And then when we come back, perhaps you could express why you despair and how you triumphantly overcome your despair and give us a sense of this cascade effect.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来时，也许你可以表达一下你为何绝望，以及你是如何胜利地克服绝望，并让我们感受到这种连锁反应的。

sentences.en: So we'll see you back in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 那么几分钟后见。

sentences.en: My dear, good, beloved wife, farewell.
sentences.zh: 我亲爱的、善良的、挚爱的妻子，永别了。

sentences.en: Live well for the times as is called eternal, but is not.
sentences.zh: 好好生活，为了那被称为永恒、实则不然的时光。

sentences.en: Bring up our, now only your, children to be fine people.
sentences.zh: 把我们的，现在只有你的，孩子们抚养成优秀的人。

sentences.en: Sell our few possessions with the help of our friends.
sentences.zh: 在朋友的帮助下卖掉我们仅有的财产。

sentences.en: God and good people will help you.
sentences.zh: 上帝和好心人会帮助你的。

sentences.en: Oh, everything I feel runs away in tears.
sentences.zh: 噢，我所感受到的一切都化作泪水流走了。

sentences.en: So I say again, live well, dear wife.
sentences.zh: 所以我再说一遍，好好生活，亲爱的妻子。

sentences.en: Farewell.
sentences.zh: 永别了。

sentences.en: Thousand, thousand.
sentences.zh: 千千万万次。

sentences.en: The last kisses from your Robert.
sentences.zh: 来自你的罗伯特的最后之吻。

sentences.en: Written in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 写于维也纳。

sentences.en: On the 9th of November at five in the morning.
sentences.zh: 11月9日凌晨五点。

sentences.en: Oh, at six.
sentences.zh: 噢，是六点。

sentences.en: It will all be over.
sentences.zh: 一切都将结束。

sentences.en: So that, Tom Holland, is described as one of the most affecting passages of 19th century German prose by the Regis Professor of History at Cambridge University, Christopher Clarke.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，这段话被剑桥大学雷吉斯历史学教授克里斯托弗·克拉克描述为19世纪德语散文中最为感人的段落之一。

sentences.en: And I don't think, Christopher, you've ever heard it read with such feeling.
sentences.zh: 而且克里斯托弗，我想你从未听过有人读得如此深情。

sentences.en: Have you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: I'm still, I'm still drying my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我还在，我还在擦眼泪。

sentences.en: It's wonderful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太美妙了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Inspector Clouseau is joined by Hair Flick.
sentences.zh: 克鲁索探长加入了弗利克先生的行列。

sentences.en: That is, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那是，没错。

sentences.en: Tom, that is, that is very cruel.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那，那太残忍了。

sentences.en: Very cruel.
sentences.zh: 太残忍了。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of listeners will be quite shocked at that remark.
sentences.zh: 而且我想很多听众会对那句话感到相当震惊。

sentences.en: I think they will.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会的。

sentences.en: I think they will.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会的。

sentences.en: But Dominic, yes.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，是的。

sentences.en: So tell us who is talking there.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们是谁在说话。

sentences.en: So we were talking about how the story was going to spread.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才在谈论故事将如何传播。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Robert Blum, who is the son of a cooper, I believe, and a seamstress or something like that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫罗伯特·布鲁姆的人，我相信他是木桶匠的儿子，母亲是裁缝之类的。

sentences.en: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我记不清了。

sentences.en: But he had become an apprentice bronze worker and then was a great autodidact and had become a pamphleteer and a poet and a radical, a German radical who believed in a united,
sentences.zh: 但他曾是一名青铜工学徒，后来是一位伟大的自学者，成为了一名小册子作者、诗人和激进派，一位相信统一、

sentences.en: liberal, democratic Germany.
sentences.zh: 自由、民主德国的德国激进派。

sentences.en: And in his trajectory is he becomes one of the faces of the German revolution and the Frankfurt parliament.
sentences.zh: 他的轨迹使他成为了德国革命和法兰克福议会的面孔之一。

sentences.en: And it all ends in tears for him because he's shot in Vienna, having written this beautiful letter so beautifully read.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，一切都以泪水告终，因为他在维也纳被枪决了，在此之前他写下了这封被读得如此动人的美丽信件。

sentences.en: So his story, Christopher, is the kind of story of what happens to the revolution in microcosm, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯托弗，他的故事是革命微观缩影的写照，不是吗？

sentences.en: High hopes, heady excitement, liberalism, and then bang, end of story, he's dead.
sentences.zh: 满怀希望、令人头晕目眩的兴奋、自由主义，然后砰，故事结束，他死了。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And for me, Robert Blum is the kind of human face of the revolution because his story captures so much of that move from the extreme euphoria of the spring days.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，罗伯特·布鲁姆是革命的人性面孔，因为他的故事捕捉到了从春日极端狂喜中转变过来的许多东西。

sentences.en: I mean, the revolution, the narrative is complicated, but it's not that complicated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，革命，这个叙事很复杂，但也没那么复杂。

sentences.en: There's a spring, there's a summer, and there's a kind of autumn and winter.
sentences.zh: 有一个春天，有一个夏天，还有一种秋天和冬天。

sentences.en: And the spring is all about everybody is out on the streets, perhaps on barricades, but perhaps simply marching or taking part in demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 春天是关于每个人都走上街头，也许是在街垒上，也许只是游行或参加示威。

sentences.en: There's an extraordinary sense of euphoria.
sentences.zh: 有一种非凡的狂喜感。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking here of one account from Berlin, from a young radical law student who says, my heart was beating so hard, I felt it was going to blow a hole in my cheSt.
sentences.zh: 我在这里想到了一份来自柏林的记录，来自一名年轻的激进法律系学生，他说，我的心跳得太厉害了，我觉得它要把我的胸口撞出一个洞来。

sentences.en: I had to get out of my room.
sentences.zh: 我必须离开我的房间。

sentences.en: So he goes out of his sort of student digs, finds himself on the street amongst thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 于是他离开了他的学生宿舍，发现自己置身于成千上万人的街道上。

sentences.en: And he says, I felt I could hear everyone else's hearts beating.
sentences.zh: 他说，我觉得我能听到其他所有人的心跳声。

sentences.en: This experience, and there's endless testimony to this, this was an experience of submersion in the collective self, of euphoria, collective euphoria,
sentences.zh: 这种体验，有无数的证词证明这一点，这是一种沉浸在集体自我中的体验，一种狂喜，集体狂喜，

sentences.en: which people remembered for the rest of their lives.
sentences.zh: 人们终生难忘。

sentences.en: So that's how the revolution starts.
sentences.zh: 这就是革命开始的方式。

sentences.en: Then in the summer comes the kind of breakdown of unity, the fractious disagreements between different bits of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 然后在夏天，统一开始破裂，革命不同部分之间出现了分裂性的分歧。

sentences.en: And Robert Blum, who's part of that spring moment and travels to the Frankfurt parliament, first to the pre-parliament and then to the parliament itself in May,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·布鲁姆，他是那个春天时刻的一部分，前往法兰克福议会，先是预备议会，然后在五月进入议会本身，

sentences.en: is full of high hopes for what's going to happen, this massive work of transformation, which he sees is about to take place.
sentences.zh: 对即将发生的事情充满希望，这是一项他认为即将进行的巨大变革工作。

sentences.en: And he joins the parliament, takes part in its business.
sentences.zh: 他加入了议会，参与了议事。

sentences.en: And in the summer, he watches the project of the revolution start to fray, to come apart.
sentences.zh: 在夏天，他看着革命的计划开始磨损、瓦解。

sentences.en: And by the autumn, he's exhausted by it and decides to go to Vienna to bring sort of fraternal greetings to the Viennese parliament.
sentences.zh: 到了秋天，他精疲力竭，决定去维也纳向维也纳议会致以兄弟般的问候。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, just as he arrives, the city is surrounded by the Austrian armies and the revolution is crushed in Austria, a very violent process,
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，就在他到达时，城市被奥地利军队包围，革命在奥地利被镇压，这是一个非常暴力的过程，

sentences.en: which results in hundreds of dead.
sentences.zh: 导致数百人死亡。

sentences.en: And Blum is arrested.
sentences.zh: 布鲁姆被捕了。

sentences.en: And although he pleads parliamentary immunity, he says, I'm a member of the Frankfurt parliament, I have immunity, they say, yeah, whatever, and execute him, as you say,
sentences.zh: 尽管他辩称拥有议会豁免权，他说，我是法兰克福议会的议员，我有豁免权，他们说，是啊，随便吧，然后像你说的，处决了他，

sentences.en: on the 9th of November.
sentences.zh: 在11月9日。

sentences.en: And there's a song about this, which tells the story of his walk to the place where he was executed.
sentences.zh: 有一首关于此的歌，讲述了他走向被处决地点时的故事。

sentences.en: And in the course of this song, the point is made, the observation is made, which we have from several sources,
sentences.zh: 在这首歌的过程中，提出了一个观点，一个我们从多个来源得知的观察结果，

sentences.en: that one of the officers commanding the firing squad noticed a tear rolling down his face
sentences.zh: 负责行刑队的军官之一注意到一滴眼泪顺着他的脸颊流下，

sentences.en: and sort of patted him on the shoulder and said, you know, keine Sorge, Blum, es ist in nur vorüber, something like that.
sentences.zh: 并拍了拍他的肩膀说，你知道，别担心，布鲁姆，一切很快就会结束，类似这样的话。

sentences.en: You know, don't worry, old chap, it'll all be over like in a jiffy, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，别担心，老兄，很快就会结束的，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know if anybody would be comforted by these words in a situation like that, but there you are.
sentences.zh: 我不知道在这种情况下是否有人会因为这些话而感到安慰，但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: And Blum turns to this man and pulls himself up to his full height, which is about five foot four, and says,
sentences.zh: 布鲁姆转向这个人，挺直了腰板，大约五英尺四英寸高，说，

sentences.en: this tear is not the tear of the parliamentary deputy, Robert Blum, it's the tear of the father and the husband.
sentences.zh: 这滴眼泪不是议员罗伯特·布鲁姆的眼泪，这是父亲和丈夫的眼泪。

sentences.en: So in other words, he insists on his right to experience a private emotion in the middle of this public event.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他坚持自己在公共事件中体验私人情感的权利。

sentences.en: And that tells us something about what a revolution is like in mid-19th century Europe.
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我们19世纪中叶欧洲的革命是什么样子的。

sentences.en: It means bringing people out of their private lives into public roles, which they've never had before.
sentences.zh: 这意味着将人们从私人生活中带入他们从未有过的公共角色中。

sentences.en: I mean, people had to discover their public selves, but they brought their private selves with them into this new public work of revolutionary activism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们必须发现他们的公共自我，但他们把私人自我带入了这项新的革命行动的公共工作中。

sentences.en: And he articulates that in this song.
sentences.zh: 他在那首歌中表达了这一点。

sentences.en: And there's a wonderful moment in this song where it says,
sentences.zh: 那首歌里有一个美妙的时刻，它说，

sentences.en: The tear for one's wife and children does not dishonor a man.
sentences.zh: 为妻子和孩子流泪并不丢人。

sentences.en: That is the ethics, if you like, of a middle class revolution.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，这就是中产阶级革命的伦理。

sentences.en: I want to go to the barricades after that.
sentences.zh: 听完那个我想去筑街垒了。

sentences.en: Tom is very moved by that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆被那个深深打动了。

sentences.en: That was so stirring.
sentences.zh: 那太令人振奋了。

sentences.en: That's the best song we've ever had on the podcast, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是我们播客里有史以来最好的歌，不是吗？

sentences.en: We don't really do singing.
sentences.zh: 我们其实不怎么唱歌。

sentences.en: I mean, we should have more singing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们应该多唱唱歌。

sentences.en: I think the last one was Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend.
sentences.zh: 我想上一首是《钻石是女孩最好的朋友》。

sentences.en: Yes, you sang that.
sentences.zh: 是的，你唱了那首。

sentences.en: But Chris's singing was, I think it's fair to say, in a very, very different league.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯的演唱，我认为公平地说，完全是另一个档次。

sentences.en: I'm happy to see that.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到这一点。

sentences.en: So, Christopher, the people who are in the revolution, are they mainly people like Robert Blum?
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯托弗，那些参与革命的人，他们主要是像罗伯特·布鲁姆那样的人吗？

sentences.en: In other words, are they high-minded, idealistic, young?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们是高尚、理想主义、年轻的人吗？

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, isn't the archetype of that is a guy called Friedrich Hecker?
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，那个人物原型难道不是一个叫弗里德里希·赫克的人吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Who kind of legal student from Heidelberg, who is, I mean, much more than Blum, seems to be the prototype for Che Guevara.
sentences.zh: 那个来自海德堡的法律系学生，他，我的意思是，比布鲁姆更像是切·格瓦拉的原型。

sentences.en: And the idea of revolutionary is romantic, has a famous beard that everyone copies.
sentences.zh: 革命者的形象是浪漫的，留着每个人都模仿的著名胡子。

sentences.en: So, can you just tell us about him?
sentences.zh: 所以，你能给我们讲讲他吗？

sentences.en: Because he seemed very romantic.
sentences.zh: 因为他看起来非常浪漫。

sentences.en: I mean, romantic in every sense of the word.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在任何意义上都是浪漫的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Hecker's a fascinating figure because Blum and Hecker had been very close and they collaborated and published in the same journals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，赫克是一个迷人的人物，因为布鲁姆和赫克曾经非常亲密，他们合作并在同一期刊上发表文章。

sentences.en: And, you know, they were part of this radical network that existed in Germany in the 1840s.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们是19世纪40年代存在于德国的那个激进网络的一部分。

sentences.en: But Hecker decides that he's had enough of the parliament.
sentences.zh: 但赫克决定他受够了议会。

sentences.en: Parliaments are slow.
sentences.zh: 议会太慢了。

sentences.en: They're talkative.
sentences.zh: 他们太爱说话了。

sentences.en: It's just talk, talk, talk.
sentences.zh: 那只是空谈，空谈，空谈。

sentences.en: And this is the great point of contrast, isn't it, between those who want constitutions and those who want.
sentences.zh: 这就是巨大的对比点，不是吗，在那些想要宪法的人和那些想要行动的人之间。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's a little bit like, you know, it's also a kind of confusion or a contrast in political timing.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是，你知道，这也是政治时机上的一种混乱或反差。

sentences.en: So, you know, on the one hand, parliaments are slow.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面，议会行动缓慢。

sentences.en: They're ponderous.
sentences.zh: 它们显得笨重。

sentences.en: They're a little bit boring.
sentences.zh: 它们还有点无聊。

sentences.en: I mean, sadly, I mean, it's just a fact about parliaments.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可悲的是，这只是关于议会的一个事实。

sentences.en: They're supposed to be boring and they should be.
sentences.zh: 它们本就应该是无聊的，也确实如此。

sentences.en: But they're full of procedural details and people have to take their time, you know, have to wait their turn to talk.
sentences.zh: 但它们充满了程序细节，人们必须花时间，你知道，必须等待轮到自己发言。

sentences.en: They mustn't speak longer than a certain time and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们发言的时间不能超过一定限度，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, it's very rule-bound.
sentences.zh: 所以，它是非常受规则约束的。

sentences.en: Whereas Hecker wants to break away from all that and go for direct action.
sentences.zh: 而赫克尔（Hecker）想要摆脱这一切，去追求直接行动。

sentences.en: So, he sets up this kind of armed insurrection in Baden, which goes horribly, horribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 于是，他在巴登发动了某种武装起义，结果却错得离谱，一败涂地。

sentences.en: He wastes a lot of people's lives, doesn't achieve anything.
sentences.zh: 他浪费了许多人的生命，却一事无成。

sentences.en: Eventually, he takes another shot at it in the following year, but then flees to, first to Switzerland and then to the United States, where he later, by the way,
sentences.zh: 最终，他在次年又尝试了一次，但随后逃往瑞士，接着又去了美国，顺便提一下，他后来在那里，

sentences.en: plays a role as a commander in the Union Army.
sentences.zh: 在联邦军队中担任了一名指挥官。

sentences.en: So, a lot of these people have very interesting, you know, afterlives after this moment of 1848.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些人中的许多在1848年这一时刻之后，都有着非常有趣的余生。

sentences.en: But, you know, for Bloom and Hecker, this is a kind of parting of the ways.
sentences.zh: 但是，对于布鲁姆（Bloom）和赫克尔来说，这是一种分道扬镳。

sentences.en: You know, Hecker represents that violent revolution by direct action, which Bloom believes is doomed to fail.
sentences.zh: 你知道，赫克尔代表了那种通过直接行动进行的暴力革命，而布鲁姆认为那注定会失败。

sentences.en: And, in fact, the fate of Hecker's escapade shows that Bloom is right.
sentences.zh: 事实上，赫克尔那次冒险的结局证明了布鲁姆是对的。

sentences.en: And, on the other hand, Bloom remains faithful to the parliament, to this process of discursive debate, of discussion, even though he knows, which is hard for a man of the left,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，布鲁姆仍然忠于议会，忠于这种话语辩论和讨论的过程，尽管他知道——这对一个左翼人士来说很难——

sentences.en: he knows that in 1848, the process of election is unlikely to produce a radical majority.
sentences.zh: 他知道在1848年，选举过程不太可能产生一个激进的多数派。

sentences.en: You have to work from a minority position and argue for, you know, for pragmatic agreements on particular policies.
sentences.zh: 你必须在少数派的立场上工作，并为，你知道，为特定政策上的务实协议进行辩论。

sentences.en: And that's what Bloom decides to do.
sentences.zh: 而这正是布鲁姆决定要做的事情。

sentences.en: So, he becomes part of that complicated business of parliament, which Hecker rejects.
sentences.zh: 所以，他成为了议会那项复杂事务的一部分，而赫克尔则拒绝了这一点。

sentences.en: But it's Hecker who ends up shaping the kind of memory of what it means to be a revolutionary because he styles.
sentences.zh: 但最终塑造了革命者形象记忆的人却是赫克尔，因为他的风格。

sentences.en: You mentioned Che Guevara before.
sentences.zh: 你之前提到了切·格瓦拉。

sentences.en: He's a very vain man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常虚荣的人。

sentences.en: He wears a broad-brimmed hat and a long beard, which comes to be known as a Hecker Bart, a Hecker beard, a red sash, baggy trousers tucked into piratical boots, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他戴着宽边帽，留着长胡子——后来被称为“赫克尔胡”（Hecker Bart）——系着红腰带，穿着塞进海盗靴里的宽松裤子，等等。

sentences.en: And so, he becomes a kind of sexy avatar of revolution, which people find disturbing and yet also perversely attractive.
sentences.zh: 因此，他成为了一种性感的革命化身，人们觉得这既令人不安，又有一种反常的吸引力。

sentences.en: And there are lots of cartoons and caricatures of him.
sentences.zh: 关于他的漫画和讽刺画有很多。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about him is even when he's being caricatured, he still kind of has a certain, you know, raw appeal.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，即使在他被讽刺的时候，他依然带有一种，你知道，原始的吸引力。

sentences.en: A sort of very basic question.
sentences.zh: 一个非常基本的问题。

sentences.en: So, these revolutions in Germany, I mean, Germany tends to end up, I mean,
sentences.zh: 那么，这些在德国的革命，我是说，德国往往最终，我是说，

sentences.en: the German speakers often tend to dominate the accounts of 1848 because you've got what's going on in Germany,
sentences.zh: 讲德语的人往往主导了对1848年的叙述，因为你有德国正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: and then you've got what's going on in Austria and the revolt in Hungary against Austria and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后你有奥地利正在发生的事情，以及匈牙利针对奥地利的起义等等。

sentences.en: But in Germany specifically, are we able to say what they want?
sentences.zh: 但在德国具体来说，我们能说出他们想要什么吗？

sentences.en: So, it's because it's there you've got a real combination of socialism, radicalism, liberalism, and nationalism, the idea of a Germany.
sentences.zh: 这是因为在那里，你真正结合了社会主义、激进主义、自由主义和民族主义，即关于“一个德国”的理念。

sentences.en: So, is there ever a sort of common, really a common program in Germany?
sentences.zh: 那么，在德国真的存在某种共同的纲领吗？

sentences.en: Or is it too confused and chaotic for that?
sentences.zh: 还是说它太混乱、太无序了，以至于无法形成？

sentences.en: Well, it's all happening so fast that people, there's not much time to establish a common program.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一切发生得太快了，人们没有太多时间去建立一个共同的纲领。

sentences.en: That's one of the difficulties.
sentences.zh: 这是困难之一。

sentences.en: And there are lots of tensions between different objectives.
sentences.zh: 而且在不同的目标之间存在许多紧张关系。

sentences.en: So, people may share, you know, many radicals like Bloom, for example, believed in parliaments.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们可能有着共同点，你知道，许多激进派，比如布鲁姆，他们相信议会。

sentences.en: They thought we do need a parliament.
sentences.zh: 他们认为我们确实需要一个议会。

sentences.en: We need the people to be represented through a process of election and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们需要人民通过选举程序等方式得到代表。

sentences.en: We can't just make it up as we go along.
sentences.zh: 我们不能边走边编。

sentences.en: On the other hand, they also wanted a social transformation.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们也想要社会变革。

sentences.en: They wanted the imbalance between labor and capital to be rebalanced so that people, the poorest strata of society, would be better seen to.
sentences.zh: 他们希望劳资之间的失衡得到重新平衡，这样社会中最贫困的阶层能得到更好的照顾。

sentences.en: They'll be in a stronger position to bargain, for example, for improvement in their conditions.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们将处于更有利的地位去争取改善自己的条件。

sentences.en: And so, they were in favor of various forms of trades, unions, or even of state intervention in the economy to support the working classes, this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们支持各种形式的工会，甚至支持国家干预经济以支持工人阶级，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But, of course, the liberals were what we would today call Thatcherites.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，自由派是我们在今天所说的“撒切尔主义者”。

sentences.en: They wanted deregulation.
sentences.zh: 他们想要去监管化。

sentences.en: They wanted the state to pull back out of the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们希望国家从经济中撤出。

sentences.en: As far as they were concerned, the private character of the economic relationships between people was an almost sacred conviction.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，人与人之间经济关系的私人性质是一种近乎神圣的信念。

sentences.en: And they said the state has no business interfering in the relationship between an employer and an employee.
sentences.zh: 他们说国家无权干涉雇主和雇员之间的关系。

sentences.en: This is a form of tyranny.
sentences.zh: 这是一种暴政。

sentences.en: And these are arguments which have not gone away, incidentally.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，这些争论至今仍未消失。

sentences.en: I mean, they're sharpened by 1848, but they have not left the world.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们在1848年变得尖锐，但它们并没有离开这个世界。

sentences.en: They're still very much at the center of our politics, which is another reason for taking an interest in this very tumultuous episode.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然处于我们政治的核心，这也是关注这一非常动荡的事件的另一个原因。

sentences.en: So, there are many different, you know, agendas maturing in that respect, trying to balance social and political reforMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这方面有许多不同的，你知道，议程正在成熟，试图平衡社会和政治改革。

sentences.en: And at the same time, there's this question of the nation, because there is no German nation state.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，存在着民族的问题，因为当时没有德国民族国家。

sentences.en: There are 39 different states.
sentences.zh: 有39个不同的邦国。

sentences.en: But a German parliament does form, and this is a remarkable thing.
sentences.zh: 但一个德国议会确实形成了，这是一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: It doesn't happen in Italy.
sentences.zh: 这在意大利没有发生。

sentences.en: But in Germany, a parliament forms to resolve the future character of a nation that does not exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但在德国，一个议会成立了，旨在解决一个尚不存在的国家的未来性质。

sentences.en: I mean, that is an extraordinary state of affairs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是一种非同寻常的状况。

sentences.en: Of course, there is no parliamentary building to put this parliament in.
sentences.zh: 当然，没有议会大厦来容纳这个议会。

sentences.en: So, it's put in a church, the St. Paul's Church of Frankfurt, a beautiful, round 18th century church, a very fine building.
sentences.zh: 所以，它被安置在法兰克福的圣保罗教堂里，那是一座美丽的、圆形的18世纪教堂，是一座非常精美的建筑。

sentences.en: And it's decorated with the red, black, and gold tricolor of the German Revolution.
sentences.zh: 它装饰着德国革命的红、黑、金三色旗。

sentences.en: And it's there to discuss the affairs of the German nation, of a German nation state that does not yet exiSt.
sentences.zh: 它在那里讨论德国民族的事务，讨论一个尚不存在的德国民族国家的事务。

sentences.en: So, what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么，发生了什么？

sentences.en: What happens is people come up with endless proposals and disagreements.
sentences.zh: 发生的是人们提出了无穷无尽的提案和分歧。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to get agreements on anything.
sentences.zh: 很难在任何事情上达成一致。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's a little bit like the EU today.
sentences.zh: 当然，这有点像今天的欧盟。

sentences.en: While this imaginary Germany is sort of trying to make decisions about its future,
sentences.zh: 当这个想象中的德国试图就其未来做出决定时，

sentences.en: that the individual territorial states, Prussia, Saxony, Bavaria, Württemberg, all the rest of the 39 of them, have not gone away.
sentences.zh: 那些独立的领土邦国——普鲁士、萨克森、巴伐利亚、符腾堡，以及其他所有39个邦国——并没有消失。

sentences.en: Prussia very much takes the initiative again by the early autumn of 1848 and starts doing deals over issues which are of great importance to the German national movement.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士在1848年初秋再次占据了主动，并开始就对德国民族运动至关重要的问题进行交易。

sentences.en: And that is one of the things that leads to the collapse of public esteem for and trust in and belief in the parliament at Frankfurt
sentences.zh: 而导致法兰克福议会的公众声望、信任和信念崩溃的原因之一，

sentences.en: is the fact that Prussia seems to be in a position to defend the interests of the German nation better than the Frankfurt parliament is.
sentences.zh: 就是普鲁士似乎比法兰克福议会更有能力捍卫德国民族的利益。

sentences.en: After all, the Frankfurt parliament has no army.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，法兰克福议会没有军队。

sentences.en: It has a tiny sort of shrunken bureaucracy, but it has no means of projecting power or of making people do what it wants them to.
sentences.zh: 它只有一个微小的、萎缩的官僚机构，但它没有手段去投射权力，也没有手段让人们服从它的意愿。

sentences.en: So, under the pressure of all that sort of powerlessness, it starts to fray and it starts to wane as a presence in people's minds.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那种无力感的压力下，它开始磨损，作为人们心中的存在感也开始减弱。

sentences.en: Just before we come to the backlash, can I ask a question that I know a lot of British reviewers have already commented on?
sentences.zh: 在我们谈到反弹之前，我可以问一个我知道很多英国评论家已经评论过的问题吗？

sentences.en: Why not Britain?
sentences.zh: 为什么不是英国？

sentences.en: So, in other words, now you will say, you might say, well, there's a big chartist meeting in Kennington or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，现在你会说，你可能会说，嗯，在肯宁顿有一个大型宪章运动集会什么的。

sentences.en: But I mean, the truth of the matter is 1848 is not a date conjured within Britain and Britain does look in that regard like a bit of an exception.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，事实是1848年并不是一个在英国引发的日期，在这方面，英国看起来确实有点例外。

sentences.en: Now, is that too strong or are you going to...
sentences.zh: 现在，这样说太绝对了吗，还是你打算……

sentences.en: No, it's not too strong.
sentences.zh: 不，这并不绝对。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 这是事实。

sentences.en: I mean, Britain, there is no revolution on the British mainland or in Ireland, which is where a tumult had also been expected.
sentences.zh: 我是说，英国，在英国本土或爱尔兰没有发生革命，而那里也曾被预期会发生骚乱。

sentences.en: I mean, Ireland was seen as the most tumultuous part of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我是说，爱尔兰被视为联合王国中最动荡的部分。

sentences.en: And that is a very interesting and important fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣且重要的事实。

sentences.en: It's interesting in this connection to read the Sydney Morning Herald down in Australia, where I come from.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，阅读澳大利亚——我来自那里——的《悉尼先驱晨报》很有趣。

sentences.en: I come from Sydney.
sentences.zh: 我来自悉尼。

sentences.en: And it's still going strong, the Sydney Morning Herald.
sentences.zh: 《悉尼先驱晨报》至今仍在强劲发展。

sentences.en: But anyway, in the context of 1848, they had to wait a long time to get the news.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，在1848年的背景下，他们不得不等待很长时间才能得到消息。

sentences.en: I mean, it was months and months and months before the news reached Sydney.
sentences.zh: 我是说，消息传到悉尼花了几个月又几个月的时间。

sentences.en: But when they commented on this, they said, why have things been so quiet in the motherland, meaning Britain,
sentences.zh: 但当他们评论这件事时，他们说，为什么母国（指英国）的情况如此平静，

sentences.en: whereas France and Germany and Italy and so on have experienced these sanguinary revolutions.
sentences.zh: 而法国、德国和意大利等地却经历了这些血腥的革命。

sentences.en: And the good burgers of the Sydney Morning Herald conclude, well, the reason is because when you have colonies,
sentences.zh: 《悉尼先驱晨报》的优秀市民们得出结论，嗯，原因是因为当你拥有殖民地时，

sentences.en: you can take all your troublemakers and push them out to the skirts of empire, to the outskirts of empire.
sentences.zh: 你可以把你所有的麻烦制造者都赶到帝国的边缘，赶到帝国的边远地区。

sentences.en: In other words, here in Sydney.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就在悉尼这里。

sentences.en: So we're getting all the troublemakers, the sons of free Ireland.
sentences.zh: 所以我们接收了所有的麻烦制造者，自由爱尔兰的子民。

sentences.en: And, you know, anybody who's sort of drawn the attention of the police in Ireland winds up in Australia on some kind of transportation charge.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，任何引起爱尔兰警方注意的人，最终都会因为某种流放指控而出现在澳大利亚。

sentences.en: So we end up, as it were, bearing the consequences.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终，可以说，承担了后果。

sentences.en: That's not really the reason, surely.
sentences.zh: 那肯定不是真正的原因吧。

sentences.en: It's part of the reason.
sentences.zh: 这是部分原因。

sentences.en: There are several reasons.
sentences.zh: 有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is, I mean, that Ireland obviously was coming to the end of an absolutely unexampled demographic shock in the form of the Irish famine.
sentences.zh: 其一，我是说，爱尔兰显然正处于一场绝对前所未有的、以爱尔兰大饥荒形式出现的人口冲击的末尾。

sentences.en: Because even then you quote this astonishing thing that the Prussians are sending inspectors to Ireland to see how you repress a revolution.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在那时，你引用了这件令人震惊的事：普鲁士人正在派遣视察员到爱尔兰，看看你们是如何镇压革命的。

sentences.en: Well, this is another part of the story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是故事的另一部分。

sentences.en: See, there are multiple reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 看，这有多种原因。

sentences.en: One is, it really is true that the British have been quite good at selecting key troublemakers and moving them out of the zone of trouble,
sentences.zh: 其一，英国人确实非常擅长挑选关键的麻烦制造者，并将他们从动乱区域移走，

sentences.en: mainly through transportation, partly to Australia and partly to South Africa, to the Cape Colony.
sentences.zh: 主要是通过流放，部分流放到澳大利亚，部分流放到南非的开普殖民地。

sentences.en: And in fact, that practice leads to movements in both those places against the further transportation of convicts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种做法导致了这两个地方都出现了反对继续流放罪犯的运动。

sentences.en: So it's partly that.
sentences.zh: 所以部分原因是这个。

sentences.en: It's partly the famine in Ireland, which obviously areas which are suffering from very serious hunger of that kind,
sentences.zh: 部分原因是爱尔兰的饥荒，显然，那些遭受严重饥饿的地区，

sentences.en: and we see it elsewhere in Europe as well, don't become active during the revolution because people are just too depleted.
sentences.zh: 我们在欧洲其他地方也看到了这一点，在革命期间并没有变得活跃，因为人们已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And then finally, it's the fact that Britain is the most robustly policed country in Europe by a very large margin.
sentences.zh: 最后，事实是英国是欧洲警力最强大的国家，优势非常明显。

sentences.en: And the Prussians recognize this.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士人意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And that's why they send in the summer of 1848, they send a fact finding group to London in the first instance,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们在1848年夏天，首先派遣了一个事实调查小组到伦敦，

sentences.en: but then to Dublin, to Corp and other locations to find out what are the British getting right?
sentences.zh: 然后又去了都柏林、科克和其他地点，去找出英国人做对了什么？

sentences.en: And how can we, the Prussians, get better at policing our own population?
sentences.zh: 我们普鲁士人怎样才能更好地管理我们自己的人口？

sentences.en: Indeed, they do introduce various changes to Prussian policing on the back of what they find out about British policing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们确实根据从英国警务中学到的东西，对普鲁士的警务进行了一些改革。

sentences.en: So it's a combination of all those different things, and also the fact that Britain is able to keep the price of stapled goods down fairly low during 1848
sentences.zh: 所以这是所有这些不同因素的结合，还有这样一个事实：在1848年期间，英国能够通过拆除英国边远殖民地（如牙买加）的关税保护，或通过减轻锡兰等地的财政负担，将主食价格保持在相当低的水平。

sentences.en: by dismantling the tariff protections of Britain's outlying colonies, places like Jamaica, or by reducing the fiscal burden of places like Ceylon, for example.
sentences.zh: 而作为这些措施的结果，那些所谓的反制、如果你愿意的话，预防性的、反革命的措施，

sentences.en: And as a result of that, of those measures, those sort of counter, if you like, prophylactic, counter-revolutionary measures,
sentences.zh: 你看到在那些外围地点中的几个爆发了动乱。

sentences.en: you see unrest break out on several of those peripheral locations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，锡兰在1848-49年发生了针对英国统治结构的大规模起义。

sentences.en: You know, Ceylon has a massive uprising against the British, the structures of British rule in 1848-49.
sentences.zh: 牙买加发生了动荡，在大英帝国边缘的其他许多地方也出现了不安。

sentences.en: There are upheavals in Jamaica and unrest in along many other parts of the periphery of the British, of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可以说存在一个“英国的1848年”，只是不在英国本土。

sentences.en: So one could say there's a British 1848, just not in Britain.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 因为你刚才说了，我是说，你讲述了英国在爱奥尼亚群岛镇压革命的非凡故事。

sentences.en: Because you all said that, I mean, you tell the extraordinary story of British repression of revolution in the Ionian Islands.
sentences.zh: 那是在希腊，也就是科孚岛等地。

sentences.en: It's in Greece, so Corfu and so on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个引人入胜的故事，因为，你知道，那是一小串七个小岛。

sentences.en: Well, that's a fascinating story, because, you know, it's a little scatter of seven tiny islands.
sentences.zh: 而在1849年特别重要的一个是凯法利尼亚岛。

sentences.en: And the one that's particularly important in 1849 is Kefalonia.
sentences.zh: 在那个岛上，发生了一场农村起义，被英国当局以典型的野蛮手段镇压了。

sentences.en: And on that island, there is a sort of rural uprising, which is put down with exemplary savagery by the British authorities.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有趣的例子，因为，你知道，当我在学校时，我们被告知那个问题的答案，

sentences.en: And I think it's quite an interesting example, because, you know, when I was at school, we were told the answer to that question,
sentences.zh: 即为什么英国没有发生革命，是因为英国已经足够自由，人们对改革的渴望已经得到满足，

sentences.en: why wasn't there a revolution in Britain, was that Britain was already so liberal that people's desire for reform was already satiated,
sentences.zh: 多亏了1832年的光荣改革法案等等。

sentences.en: thanks to the Glorious Reform Act of 1832 and so on.
sentences.zh: 而宪章派，好吧，他们是，你知道，一个为了改革而不是为了革命的运动。

sentences.en: And the Chartists were, OK, well, they were, you know, a movement for reform, not for revolution.
sentences.zh: 你的宪章派是一个理智的人，他宁愿回家和妻子喝茶，也不愿去放火烧别人的房子，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And your Chartist was a sensible kind of fellow who would rather go home and have tea with his wife than set fire to someone else's house and this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是当时提出的论点。

sentences.en: And so those are the arguments that were made.
sentences.zh: 而且正是英国制度的自由拯救了英国免于革命。

sentences.en: And that it was it was the liberality of British institutions that saved Britain from revolution.
sentences.zh: 但在爱奥尼亚群岛，我们并没有看到太多的自由。

sentences.en: But on the Ionian Islands, we don't see too much liberality.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是大量的鞭刑和绞刑。

sentences.en: What we see is a lot of flogging and hanging.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，关于英国人如何处理凯法利尼亚这场起义，在欧洲引发了一场丑闻。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's a, you know, there's a kind of Europe wide scandal over how the British handled this uprising in Kefalonia.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的例子，你知道，当你真正看到英国当局面对那种在整个欧洲大陆爆发的局部动乱时，

sentences.en: And so that's an interesting example of, you know, when you actually do see British authorities facing a local tumult of the kind that broke out across the continent.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有看到他们的行为与奥地利人、普鲁士人和其他欧洲国家有什么不同。

sentences.en: And we don't see that they behave more or less as the Austrians and the Prussians and other European states do.
sentences.zh: 但是，你所学的传统故事难道一点真实成分都没有吗？

sentences.en: But is there no element of truth to the traditional story that you were taught?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think there is an element of truth.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中确实有真实成分。

sentences.en: And the element of truth, and it connects that argument about liberality with the argument about policing.
sentences.zh: 而这一真实成分，将关于自由的论点与关于治安的论点联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And that is that, you know, when the mass meeting on Kennington Common took place that Dominic referred to, there's, you know, the mass meeting of Chartists.
sentences.zh: 那就是，你知道，当多米尼克提到的肯宁顿公地群众大会召开时，那是宪章派的群众大会。

sentences.en: I mean, it was very alarming at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时这非常令人警觉。

sentences.en: People worried about what would happen.
sentences.zh: 人们担心会发生什么。

sentences.en: And in fact, Metternich, who was on his way out of Europe, fleeing to Britain, stopped in Rotterdam for a few days because they were waiting out the news.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时正要离开欧洲、逃往英国的梅特涅，在鹿特丹停留了几天，因为他们正在等待消息。

sentences.en: It rained very heavily, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 雨下得很大，不是吗？

sentences.en: The rain stopped play, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，雨水中断了比赛。

sentences.en: Which is never, never a help.
sentences.zh: 这可从来都不是什么好事。

sentences.en: But in addition, 80,000 special constables turned up.
sentences.zh: 但此外，还有8万名特别警察出现了。

sentences.en: Including Gladstone.
sentences.zh: 包括格莱斯顿。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And including the future Napoleon III, who'd signed up as a special constable, was hoping to get his hands on some Chartists and give them a right drubbing.
sentences.zh: 还包括未来的拿破仑三世，他报名当了特别警察，希望能亲手抓住一些宪章派分子，狠狠地教训他们一顿。

sentences.en: Never got the chance to do that.
sentences.zh: 但他没能得到那个机会。

sentences.en: You know, but there's a commentary by a Tory at the time called Sibthorpe, sort of ultra Tory, who says that, you know, by gum,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时有一位名叫西布索普的托利党人，算是极端的托利党人，他评论说，天哪，
