sentences.en: if only those special constables had a chance to get stuck into those Chartists, they would have given them such a hiding as no man ever received something.
sentences.zh: 要是那些特别警察有机会去对付那些宪章派，他们会给他们一顿前所未有的痛打。

sentences.en: And I think he wasn't wrong.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他说得没错。

sentences.en: I mean, what's special about Britain is it could mobilize, out of its own society, counter-revolutionary forces on a scale which we don't see anywhere else in Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国的特别之处在于，它能从自身社会中动员起反革命力量，其规模在欧洲其他任何地方都看不到。

sentences.en: You know, Gizor can't summon up 80,000 special constables wielding clubs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，基佐可召集不来8万名挥舞棍棒的特别警察。

sentences.en: Because these people are volunteers, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这些人是志愿者，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: These people are volunteers.
sentences.zh: 这些人是志愿者。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're not even paid.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有报酬。

sentences.en: They want to get stuck in.
sentences.zh: 他们就是想参与其中。

sentences.en: So there's a sense in which you have a sufficiently large stakeholding element in the society to come to the defense of the current political order against those who would challenge it.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种意义上，社会中存在着足够庞大的利益相关群体，他们会站出来捍卫当前的政治秩序，对抗那些挑战它的人。

sentences.en: And talking about sort of counter-revolutionary, so, you know, it's a huge canvas to try and cover in just under an hour.
sentences.zh: 说到反革命，你知道，要在不到一小时的时间里涵盖这么宏大的主题确实很难。

sentences.en: But when we get to the sort of late summer, autumn, there is this backlash.
sentences.zh: 但当我们进入夏末秋初时，确实出现了这种反弹。

sentences.en: Now, do you think that was, you know, the Austrians sending in the troops, the French turn to the guy who becomes Napoleon III and so on and so forth?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为那是必然的吗？比如奥地利派兵，法国转向后来成为拿破仑三世的那个人等等？

sentences.en: Do you think ultimately that was inevitable?
sentences.zh: 你认为最终那是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I know historians were never allowed to talk about things being inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我知道历史学家从不被允许谈论事情是不可避免的。

sentences.en: But do you think that was always likely to happen,
sentences.zh: 但你认为那总是很可能发生的吗，

sentences.en: that the forces of counter-reaction were always too strong and that the Robert Blooms of this world were never really going to get what they wanted?
sentences.zh: 反动力量总是太强大，而像罗伯特·布鲁姆这样的人注定无法实现他们的愿望？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question when you put it like that.
sentences.zh: 当你这样提问时，这真是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Was it always going to happen that way?
sentences.zh: 事情总是会那样发展吗？

sentences.en: I mean, some of these outcomes are profoundly surprising.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一些结果令人深感意外。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that someone like Napoleon III, well, he's not Napoleon III yet,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，像拿破仑三世这样的人——好吧，他当时还不是拿破仑三世——

sentences.en: but the fact that the man who will become Emperor Napoleon III is voted president of the republic in December 1848,
sentences.zh: 但那个后来成为拿破仑三世皇帝的人，在1848年12月被选为共和国总统，

sentences.en: which is one of the death blows to the revolutionary movement in Paris and in France as a whole.
sentences.zh: 这对巴黎乃至整个法国的革命运动来说，都是致命一击。

sentences.en: Well, that's actually a very unexpected and rather odd outcome because, you know, in the 1830s and 40s, he'd been a figure of ridicule.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这实际上是一个非常出人意料且相当奇怪的结果，因为你知道，在19世纪30和40年代，他一直是个笑柄。

sentences.en: So, he kind of comes from nowhere, from left field.
sentences.zh: 所以，他算是横空出世，出人意料。

sentences.en: He's a bit like Trump.
sentences.zh: 他有点像特朗普。

sentences.en: In fact, in many ways, he is a Trumpian kind of character.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在很多方面，他确实是一个特朗普式的人物。

sentences.en: So, there's nothing inevitable about that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这没什么不可避免的。

sentences.en: What seemed at the time to be unlikely was the rapid success of the revolutions.
sentences.zh: 当时看起来不太可能的是革命的迅速成功。

sentences.en: So, revolutions are, if you like, sequences of very unlikely events.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，革命是一系列极不可能发生的事件。

sentences.en: It's unlikeliness following unlikeliness following unlikeliness.
sentences.zh: 是一个接一个的不可能事件。

sentences.en: And so, nothing in a way about any of this was particularly likely.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，这一切并没有什么特别可能发生的。

sentences.en: But, nevertheless, in retrospect, obviously, it becomes clear that the forces of the Ancien Regime, which is not really the right term for them,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，回顾过去，显然很清楚，旧制度的力量——虽然这并不是形容它们的正确术语——

sentences.en: but the forces of order that had been challenged by the revolution, they had cards up their sleeves,
sentences.zh: 但那些被革命挑战的秩序力量，他们手里还有底牌，

sentences.en: more cards up their sleeves than perhaps they seemed to when the revolution was initially in the full flush of its success.
sentences.zh: 比革命最初处于成功巅峰时看起来要多得多的底牌。

sentences.en: They had loyal armed forces.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有忠诚的武装部队。

sentences.en: That was one of the most important things.
sentences.zh: 这是最重要的事情之一。

sentences.en: And another sort of thing that I think they didn't know themselves was they had the support of a surprisingly large part of the population.
sentences.zh: 还有一点我认为他们自己也没意识到，那就是他们得到了人口中相当大一部分人的支持。

sentences.en: It seemed during the revolution that the liberals and the radicals were absolutely making the running.
sentences.zh: 革命期间，自由派和激进派似乎完全占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: All the newspapers, all the pamphlets, all the posters, all the public manifestations were for revolution of one form or another.
sentences.zh: 所有的报纸、小册子、海报、公共示威活动都是为了某种形式的革命。

sentences.en: But what emerged as the revolution began to wane was a sort of backlash of popular conservatism that no one had really known was there.
sentences.zh: 但随着革命开始衰退，出现了一种大众保守主义的反弹，这是没人真正预料到的。

sentences.en: And this is one of the great sort of discoveries for the conservatives that, you know, perhaps it's us.
sentences.zh: 这是保守派的伟大发现之一，即，也许是我们（代表了大众）。

sentences.en: This is what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们所说的。

sentences.en: Anyway, perhaps we're the ones who really know the little people.
sentences.zh: 总之，也许我们才是真正了解小人物的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The revolutions were living in a bubble, in an urban bubble.
sentences.zh: 革命者生活在一个泡沫中，一个城市泡沫中。

sentences.en: People like each other.
sentences.zh: 人们互相认同。

sentences.en: So, this is your 1968 parallel, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你提到的1968年的类比，对吧？

sentences.en: That 1968 ends with the election of Richard Nixon and the war in Vietnam continues and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 1968年以理查德·尼克松的当选告终，越南战争继续，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And, you know, when President de Gaulle calls out the people of France and actually there are more of them than they are of the people throwing cobblestones at the police, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当戴高乐总统呼吁法国人民时，实际上支持他的人比那些向警察投掷鹅卵石的人要多，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the same story.
sentences.zh: 这是同一个故事。

sentences.en: But in a way, isn't it even more primal than that?
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这难道不是更原始吗？

sentences.en: That perhaps we think of 1848 as the revolutionary year,
sentences.zh: 也许我们认为1848年是革命之年，

sentences.en: but it's also the year that gives birth perhaps to conservatism as a political force in the way that we would understand it now.
sentences.zh: 但它也是保守主义作为一种政治力量诞生的年份，以我们现在理解的方式。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: That's the complexity of 1848, that revolution and counterrevolution are born twins in the same bed.
sentences.zh: 这就是1848年的复杂之处，革命和反革命是同床异梦的孪生子。

sentences.en: That's the weird thing about 1848.
sentences.zh: 这就是1848年奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件令人着迷的事情。

sentences.en: But, of course, counterrevolution, you know, conservatism is not the same as reaction.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，反革命，你知道，保守主义并不等同于反动。

sentences.en: There are reactionaries who are saying, you know, we've got to unmake this revolution.
sentences.zh: 有一些反动派说，你知道，我们必须废除这场革命。

sentences.en: We've got to turn the clock of history back.
sentences.zh: 我们必须让历史的时钟倒转。

sentences.en: But they are in a small minority and they all fail.
sentences.zh: 但他们只是极少数，而且都失败了。

sentences.en: Whereas the conservatives who are going to shape the future are conservatives who've learned from the revolution.
sentences.zh: 而那些将塑造未来的保守派，是向革命学习过的保守派。

sentences.en: So like Bismarck being the classic.
sentences.zh: 比如俾斯麦就是一个经典。

sentences.en: Bismarck is a classic example, a man of brilliant intellect who immediately sees this revolution cannot be undone.
sentences.zh: 俾斯麦是一个典型的例子，一个才华横溢的人，他立刻看出这场革命是无法撤销的。

sentences.en: It's a new point of departure.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新的起点。

sentences.en: We've got to live with it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须接受它。

sentences.en: And anyone who tries to resuscitate the pre-revolutionary past is a fool.
sentences.zh: 任何试图复辟革命前过去的人都是傻瓜。

sentences.en: And throughout his life, he recognized that 1848 was the sort of pivotal moment in his own career.
sentences.zh: 他一生都承认，1848年是他职业生涯中的关键时刻。

sentences.en: It was the enabling moment that without it, he could never have become the person that he became because it was the revolution that allowed him to enter public life.
sentences.zh: 那是让他能够有所作为的时刻，没有它，他永远无法成为后来的他，因为正是革命让他进入了公共生活。

sentences.en: And because it unleashes the power of nationalism, right?
sentences.zh: 而且因为它释放了民族主义的力量，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it creates the idea of the nation as the main vehicle for kind of popular idealism and aspirations and crowds and modernity.
sentences.zh: 因为它创造了民族的概念，作为大众理想、愿望、群众和现代性的主要载体。

sentences.en: Nationalism is modern after 1848, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 1848年之后，民族主义才变得现代，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: Although Bismarck seems very clear that nationalism is going to have to be a managed force.
sentences.zh: 尽管俾斯麦似乎非常清楚，民族主义将不得不成为一种被管理的势力。

sentences.en: It will have to be managed by a media which is itself carefully managed and overseen.
sentences.zh: 它将不得不由一个本身受到仔细管理和监督的媒体来管理。

sentences.en: And that's the great lesson of 1848, that nationalism kind of as a free-floating potential in European society is not going to achieve very much.
sentences.zh: 这就是1848年的伟大教训，即作为欧洲社会中一种自由浮动的潜力的民族主义，是不会取得多大成就的。

sentences.en: But nationalism, when it's yoked to state power, will achieve enormous amounts.
sentences.zh: 但是，当民族主义与国家权力结合时，它将取得巨大的成就。

sentences.en: And that's what happens after 1848.
sentences.zh: 这就是1848年之后发生的事情。

sentences.en: So lots of the kind of the more radical constitutions and so on get repealed.
sentences.zh: 所以很多更激进的宪法等等都被废除了。

sentences.en: And to that extent, we could perhaps talk of the ambitions and hopes of the more radical revolutionaries failing.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们或许可以说更激进的革命者的雄心和希望失败了。

sentences.en: But one of the things that struck me in the book was that actually there are a number of constitutions in Europe that are still kind of basically current today that do reach back to 1848.
sentences.zh: 但书中的一件事让我印象深刻，那就是实际上欧洲仍有一些宪法在今天基本适用，它们可以追溯到1848年。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Switzerland, I suppose, reached back to 1847, but the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 你提到了瑞士，我想是追溯到1847年，还有荷兰。

sentences.en: And I thought the most interesting one was Denmark, which had been the kind of absolute monarchy and then becomes a kind of model liberal democracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为最有趣的是丹麦，它曾经是绝对君主制，后来变成了一种模范的自由民主国家。

sentences.en: And that constitution stays in place after 1848.
sentences.zh: 那部宪法在1848年之后一直保留了下来。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: To this day, the Danes still celebrate the day of the promulgation of that constitution, the June basic law.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，丹麦人仍在庆祝那部宪法的颁布日，即六月基本法。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, that's just one of many examples of constitutions that still survive today.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这只是今天仍然存在的众多宪法例子之一。

sentences.en: I mean, the Swiss constitution of 1848, it's not until 1848 they actually promulgated, is still in force with many amendments and so on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，1848年的瑞士宪法——直到1848年他们才真正颁布——在经过多次修正后仍然有效。

sentences.en: The Dutch constitution of 18, the revised Dutch constitution of 1849, which comes about as a result of the 1848 revolutions, those revisions are still in place.
sentences.zh: 1849年修订的荷兰宪法，是1848年革命的结果，这些修订至今仍然有效。

sentences.en: And, you know, in many ways, these, the Italians too, the Italian constitution winds up being the Piedmontese constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在很多方面，这些——意大利人也是，意大利宪法最终变成了皮埃蒙特宪法。

sentences.en: The Piedmontese constitution is issued in March 1848, the Statuto Albertino.
sentences.zh: 皮埃蒙特宪法于1848年3月颁布，即《阿尔贝蒂诺宪章》。

sentences.en: And it too survives, and bits of its language are still present in today's Italian constitution.
sentences.zh: 它也保留了下来，其部分语言至今仍存在于意大利现行宪法中。

sentences.en: And so are bits of the German constitution of 1848.
sentences.zh: 1848年德国宪法的部分内容也是如此。

sentences.en: They're still present in the Grundgesetz of today's German Federal Republic.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然存在于当今德国联邦共和国的《基本法》中。

sentences.en: So a huge amount of what was achieved in this, in the course of these revolutions, did stand the test of time and did survive.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这些革命过程中取得的巨大成就确实经受住了时间的考验并存活了下来。

sentences.en: We haven't really got time to touch it, but you also argue that modern contemporary Catholicism dates back to this time as well.
sentences.zh: 我们没有时间细说，但你也认为现代当代天主教也追溯到那个时期。

sentences.en: That's another fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个迷人的故事。

sentences.en: The Catholic Church, we don't have time for that, but it has to completely remake itself.
sentences.zh: 天主教会，我们没时间细谈，但它必须彻底重塑自己。

sentences.en: And it does in the aftermath of 1848.
sentences.zh: 它在1848年之后确实做到了。

sentences.en: And most of what we think of as the Catholic Church is actually born in that moment.
sentences.zh: 我们所认为的天主教会的大部分内容实际上都是在那一刻诞生的。

sentences.en: And your last lines, so you basically say, we're not supposed to see ourselves when we look back in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 还有你的最后几行，你基本上说，当我们回顾过去时，我们不应该看到我们自己。

sentences.en: I mean, I think Tom and I would completely agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想汤姆和我完全同意这一点。

sentences.en: However, intriguingly, you think the revolutionaries of 1848 could see themselves in us.
sentences.zh: 然而，有趣的是，你认为1848年的革命者可以在我们身上看到他们自己。

sentences.en: So the resonances between then and now, you find very striking.
sentences.zh: 所以你发现那时与现在之间的共鸣非常惊人。

sentences.en: I find them very striking.
sentences.zh: 我发现它们非常惊人。

sentences.en: And I wanted to say two things with that closing comment.
sentences.zh: 我想用那句结束语表达两件事。

sentences.en: One is that, you know, the resonances are there, and the more you think about them, the more there are, and the more persuasive they seem.
sentences.zh: 一是，你知道，共鸣确实存在，你思考得越多，共鸣就越多，它们看起来就越有说服力。

sentences.en: And the second thing is that those people were smart.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，那些人很聪明。

sentences.en: It's easy to think of people in the past as crackpots with flawed schemes and so on, especially when their schemes don't come off.
sentences.zh: 很容易把过去的人看作是带着有缺陷计划的怪人，尤其是当他们的计划没有实现时。

sentences.en: But actually, they were incredibly thoughtful and intelligent people.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们是非常深思熟虑和聪明的人。

sentences.en: They were at least as smart as us.
sentences.zh: 他们至少和我们一样聪明。

sentences.en: They were thinking about the future.
sentences.zh: 他们在思考未来。

sentences.en: So they were thinking about us.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在思考我们。

sentences.en: I mean, even though they didn't know us individually, sadly for them, but nevertheless, they were thinking about the future.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尽管他们不认识我们个人，这对他们来说很遗憾，但无论如何，他们确实在思考未来。

sentences.en: And they were doing that in a very interesting, adventurous, and, you know, intellectually resourceful way.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是以一种非常有趣、冒险且在智力上足智多谋的方式在做这件事。

sentences.en: And that's one of the real fascinations of this revolution, that it was like a kind of wild experimental laboratory.
sentences.zh: 这就是这场革命真正令人着迷的地方之一，它就像一个疯狂的实验实验室。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's why I think it repays our attention today.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就是为什么我认为它值得我们今天关注。

sentences.en: And that's why the book really is an attempt to refute a comment made by a very beloved teacher, actually, a history teacher at school,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这本书实际上试图反驳一位我很敬爱的老师——其实是学校的一位历史老师——所发表的评论，

sentences.en: who announced that when we were doing 1848, he said to us, boys, the 1848 revolutions are complicated and they're a failure.
sentences.zh: 他在我们学习1848年历史时宣布说：孩子们，1848年革命很复杂，而且是一场失败。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking that's a very unattractive combination.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，这是一个非常糟糕的组合。

sentences.en: And the book is really a document, my discovery of how wrong that is.
sentences.zh: 这本书实际上是一份记录，记录了我发现这种说法是多么错误。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not entirely wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它并不完全错误。

sentences.en: They are complicated, but they're not a failure.
sentences.zh: 它们确实很复杂，但它们并不是失败。

sentences.en: And they're very, very interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且它们非常、非常有趣。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, the book is Revolutionary Spring, Fighting for a New World, 1848 to 1849.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这本书是《革命之春：为新世界而战，1848至1849年》。

sentences.en: It's a huge book, but enormously readable.
sentences.zh: 这是一本大部头，但非常易读。

sentences.en: And I can't recommend it enough.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐。

sentences.en: Tom, you enjoyed reading it, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你读得很开心，对吧？

sentences.en: I really did.
sentences.zh: 我确实很喜欢。

sentences.en: As my Twitter followers will know, I quoted vast chunks of it.
sentences.zh: 正如我的推特粉丝所知，我引用了书中大量的片段。

sentences.en: Really great.
sentences.zh: 真的很棒。

sentences.en: So, Christopher, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯托弗，非常感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: Thank you for enduring Tom's shocking French accent in the first half.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家忍受了汤姆在上半场那令人震惊的法语口音。

sentences.en: And Dominic's, I mean, appalling German accent.
sentences.zh: 还有多米尼克的，我是说，那糟糕透顶的德语口音。

sentences.en: But I think, no, no, Christopher agreed that you were very harsh on it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，不，不，克里斯托弗同意你们对他太苛刻了。

sentences.en: No, I was deeply moved by both performances.
sentences.zh: 不，我被这两场表演深深打动了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Well, you did a bit of singing yourself, which is always good on the rest of its history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你自己也唱了几句，这对《历史余谈》来说总是件好事。

sentences.en: Do you have a revolutionary song from 1848 that you could take us out with?
sentences.zh: 你有什么1848年的革命歌曲可以为我们收尾吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes, there's a nice one that the poet Freilichkart did in the form of a translation of Robbie Burns' song, For All That, A Man's A Man, For All That.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有的，诗人弗莱利希卡特曾把罗伯特·彭斯的《尽管如此，人终究是人》翻译成了一首很棒的歌。

sentences.en: He translated it into really beautiful German.
sentences.zh: 他把它翻译成了非常优美的德语。

sentences.en: And it's really one of the loveliest songs of 1848.
sentences.zh: 这确实是1848年最可爱的歌曲之一。

sentences.en: Take it away.
sentences.zh: 请开始你的表演。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Goodbye, everyone.
sentences.zh: 再见，各位。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest Is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史余谈》。
